Morning light pooled in through the windows across the hardwood floor like honey brew spilled from a warm spoon. Mydei sat cross-legged on the couch, his hands working through Augusta’s hair as she sat between his knees, holding a small compact mirror to watch what he was doing. 

“Hold still, babygirl,” he murmured, parting the next section of her fiery locks. 

Augusta squirmed with a little giggle. “It tickles.”

“Beauty comes with a price,” he teased, meeting her eyes through the mirror. He pressed a soft kiss to the top of her head. “Besides, we both know you like it when Mama does your hair.”

“Mhm!” she exclaimed, nodding a little sleepily. 

Mydei smiled to himself, weaving each strand with care. “You have music today, don’t you?”

“Uh-huh! Miss Tribios says I get to play the triangle again!” She tilted her head proudly, clearly a little more awake now. “Last week, I hit it too hard and it flew across the floor.”

Mydei snorted. “How about we aim to keep it in your hands today, hm?”

Augusta giggled, the sound wrapping around him like warmth. Moments like these were what made everyday worth it. It was just the two of them in the sun-drenched room, and the steady rhythm of the routine they’d created. 

Mydei secured the braid once it was done with a tiny blue tie she’d picked herself. “There,” he said, turning her gently so she could see herself in the mirror. “Perfect.”

She gasped. “I look like a princess!”

“You are a princess,” he said, tapping her nose gently in the way that made her little face scrunch up. 

By the time he’d packed her snack and double-checked her folder, his daughter was tugging on her shoes by the door. 

“Mama,” she asked, voice suddenly becoming cautious. “Can I have a cookie when I come home today?”

Mydei’s lips almost twitched into a smile. “We’ll see… maybe if you don’t throw your triangle across the floor today,” he said, adjusting the strap of her backpack and ushering her outside as she mumbled a little determined I’m gonna be careful, I promise . 

The school wasn’t far from their home atop the bakery. He walked her to school like he always did with her skipping just ahead of him and sometimes stopping to look at something shiny or chase a butterfly that Mydei would fondly roll his eyes and call her back over. 

Mydei crouched down to kiss her goodbye and watched her dash through the gates over to where her teacher was waiting for the children. He smiled a little to himself. For a little while, it helped him forget about the ache he carried beneath his ribs, but he told himself that this was all he needed. That Augusta was all he cared about. 

He turned back toward the bakery with his hands in his coat packets, the silence following him home a little louder than he expected. 

☼

The scent of fresh bread and espresso filled the bakery when Cipher breezed in, shaking the last of the morning dew from her coat. She was already talking before Mydei could even hand her a cup of coffee. 

“Okay so, Cassie wants peonies, do you know how much peonies cost in the off-season? I swear I’m going to have to sell my soul or yours . Yours is probably worth more,” She said, plopping down at the counter. “Also, apparently the reception hall has rules about catering and outside desserts, which is ridiculous by the way because why would I let anyone else make our cake when you exist?”

Mydei fondly rolled his eyes, sliding a cup of coffee and a pastry across the counter, letting Cipher fill the space with her chatter. “Maybe you should elope,” he suggested mildly. 

Cipher gasped as though mortally wounded, hand flying to her chest. “And deny everyone the joy of seeing us look devastatingly good together? Absolutely not! ” 

The bell over the door chimed again, and this time Castorice stepped in, cheeks slightly flushed from the heat. Cipher’s eye immediately softened at the sight of her fiancee, a fond smile tugging at her lips. 

“You’re late, princess homebody,” she teased.

Castorice leaned over to press a kiss to her cheek. “Some of us have classes that run long. Good morning, Mydei.”

“Morning,” Mydei responded, not missing the way Cipher’s hands were already on her waist. “You’re going to scare the customers away.”

“We’ll tone it down,” Cipher lied cheerfully. 

Castorice lingered near the counter, eyes darting toward Cipher before turning to Mydei a little hesitantly. “Oh, I ran into Professor Anaxa this morning. He mentioned that Phainon took a position at the University.” 

Cipher’s brows shot up, a smirk forming almost instantly. “Well, well, well, isn’t that interesting~, the universe is finally spicing up your life.” 

Castorice elbowed her lightly, shooting her a look. “ Cifera .”

“Whaaat? I’m just saying,” she pouted, though her tone was still amused. “Our little Prince is due for some fun~,”

The words hung in the air and Mydei’s hands still around the bowl he was holding, his gaze fixed on the espresso beans in front of him. Phainon was… back? His— No, not his —Phainon, but he was back and working at the University, which meant that this could be permanent.

“It’s none of my concern,” he said after a beat, voice surprisingly even. “We haven’t spoken in years.”

Cipher tilted her head, clearly holding back more commentary. Castorice gave a small nod, knowing that it was time to drop the subject but not without adding, "I just thought you deserved to know…for her.”

But still, not long after their conversation shifted back to florists and seating charts, Mydei felt the name echo in the back of his mind, turning over and over until it was against his ribs like something sharp. He pulled another shot of espresso, hoping the heat in his hands would keep him from unraveling. 

The rest of the day had been uneventful, customers came and went, but none of them were him . Mydei didn’t even know what he was hoping would happen. Did he want Phainon to walk in through those doors? Did he want Phainon to see Augusta and wonder why Mydei never told him? Would he be angry? Would he resent Mydei from keeping this secret from him?

The evening had crept up on him and the bakery was quiet except for the hum of the refrigerator and the soft pitter patter of rain against the windows. Mydei moved through his usual closing routine without much thought. He wiped down counters, stacked chairs, and counted the register. Augusta sat on a stool near the display case, chin propped on her hands as she weighed the monumental decision of which cookie she wanted after dinner from what was left. 

“Chocolate chip or snickerdoodle…” she muttered, eyes narrowed as if the answer would magically come to her before she perked up and looked toward him. “Mama, can I have two?”

“Uh-uh, only one,” he reminded her, ruffling her hair as he passed by. “Choose wisely.”

She sighed, bottom lip sticking out slightly before going back to deliberating. Mydei watched her for a moment longer than necessary, telling himself that it didn’t matter who had come to the city. 

“I want chocolate chip!” Augusta announced, finally having made her decision. 

Yeah. It didn’t matter at all. 

☼

A few nights later, Augusta lay tucked beneath her blankets, hair loose and splayed across the pillow. She was clearly fighting sleep, still talking in a slurred, dreamy tone about her day, how she wished they had music class again, how her lunch was yummy, that she’d eaten her pomegranate seeds because they’re her favourite, and how Miss Tribios’ shoes squeaked on the floor. 

Mydei sat at the edge of her bed, running his fingers gently through her hair. “You’re supposed to be sleeping, little one,” he murmured. 

“I’m not… tired,” she yawned, blinking heavily. 

“Mm,” he smoothed a curl behind her ear. 

Her voice faded as her eyes finally slipped closed, breath evening out. Mydei smiled, leaning over to press a kiss against her temple. His mind drifted back to before she was born, back to the day when Phainon had gotten that opportunity to study abroad. They weren’t anything but friends back then. Friends who had been dancing around each other for ages. Friends who had shared a night together and never spoke a word about it. 

Phainon’s life was just beginning. He was getting out of that small town and building something for himself. He was excited to go, there were so many things he wanted to learn. Mydei didn’t want to be the reason he stayed. He’d convinced himself it was better this way, kinder to let him go. 

But he wondered if that kindness had only been cowardice in disguise. 

He slipped into his own room, leaving the door slightly ajar just in case his daughter had a nightmare and wanted to sleep in his room. He changed into something comfortable before sliding beneath the sheets. The quiet left too much space for thought. 

He’d been so caught up in thinking about the Phainon he knew that he didn’t consider the possibility that Phainon could have settled down with someone. Someone who knew how to smile, someone who could keep up with his boundless energy. Someone who got to be there for all the moments Mydei wasn’t. 

“ Shit ,” he cursed under his breath, throwing an arm across his face. He let out a sigh, staring up at the ceiling for a long time before caving, reaching for his phone on the nightstand. If he was going to ask, it would be to someone who wasn’t going to turn it into gossip. 

His thumbs hovered for a second before typing a short message to Castorice: 

If you’ve seen him around, did he seem… happy?

The reply came a few minutes later:

Mydei… 

He seemed fine. I don’t know if happy’s the word. 

Are you okay?

Mydei hesitated for a moment. 

Yeah. Just curious. 

Don’t make a thing of it 

Castorice’s typing dots appeared, vanished, and then returned. 

Alright. I won’t. But… you’d tell me if this

 was more than curiosity, right?

I’m here for you, Mydei. Cipher is too 

Mydei stared at the screen for a long moment. 

Goodnight, Cas 

☼

Augusta sat perched on one of the stools at the counter, swinging her legs and occasionally sipping warm milk from a mug nearly as big as her hands. A few crumbs clung to her cheek from the pastry Mydei let her have earlier. 

“Can I have another one?” she asked, already eyeing the tray cooling on the rack. 

Mydei shook his head as he slid a tray of fresh croissants into the display case, watching as she stuck her bottom lip out in a little pout. Something that always reminded Mydei of him . “Don’t think I don’t know you’re planning to charm the customers into sharing theirs.”

August grinned, letting out a soft “hee”. “Maybe they’ll think I’m cute.”

“They’ll be right” he said, smoothing a curl behind her ear as he passed. He grabbed a cloth and cleaning spray before wiping down some of the tables. 

The bell over the door chimed and Gorgo swept in, her coat neatly buttoned and her hair pulled back into a bun. “I thought I’d find you here,” she said, her voice brisk but with a softness reserved for Augusta. “And there’s my little grandbaby.”

Augusta’s face lit up. “Grandma!!” She nearly sloshed her milk in her rush to hug her. 

Gorgo kissed her forehead, then gave Mydei a once-over that was equally affectionate and assessing. “Something is on your mind, my son.” 

“It’s just been busy, mother.”

She settled onto the stool next to Augusta, accepting the cup of coffee Mydei poured without asking. “I was in the neighbourhood. Thought I’d stop by and check in. How’s business?”

Mydei studied her for a moment. She was holding back, he knew his mother well enough to know that. “Steady, weekends are always busier,” he replied, glancing toward the front where a couple of regulars sat with their lattes. 

His daughter, meanwhile, was enthusiastically recounting the morning, her story reading plans for later, and the new colouring book she was finally going to open. Gorgo listened with patience, nodding and adding the occasional “mhmm” or “you don’t say.” 

When the rush eased, Mydei joined them at the counter, closing his eyes for a moment. 

“You know who I ran into the other day?” Gorgo began and Mydei hummed in response, eyes still closed. “Phainon.” 

There it was . The reason she’d come in today. 

Mydei opened his eyes to meet her gaze. 

“Who’s Phainon?” Augusta asked curiously, looking between them. 

“No one, sweetheart,” Mydei responded, shooting his mother a look, firm but not unkind. 

“But—” Augusta began. 

“Hey, little star, why don’t we go out for lunch, hm? Just us girls,” Gorgo suggested. 

Augusta gasped, already bouncing on her feet. “Mama, Can I?!” 

Mydei chuckled before nodding and his daughter was already off to grab her things. When she was out of earshot, he turned to his mother. 

“Don’t you think he deserves to know?” Gorgo began, lowering her voice. 

He didn’t look at her, focusing instead on drying some cups. “It’s not that simple.”

“It’s exactly that simple, Mydeimos,” she countered. “She’s his daughter.”

She’s mine,” Mydei said, sharper than he intended. He sighed. “Telling him would change everything. I’m not sure I want that for her.”

Gorgo pursed her lips, her expression unreadable “Or perhaps you’re unsure if you want that for yourself.”

Mydei paused. Was it selfish? Before he could respond, Augusta came bounding back with a little bag and new lavender clip tucked in her hair. “I’m ready!”

“Alright, my little star, let’s head out.”

Mydei forced a smile as Gorgo took her hands, tucking the conversation away as quickly as it had begun. He couldn’t keep thinking about this. 

☼

Later in the week, Mydei found himself walking through the lakeside market with Castorice at his side, a break from his usual routine. The bakery was closed for the morning and Augusta was at school. Castorice was a little more talkative today, gesturing with one hand while the other clutched a to-go cup from a nearby cafe that Mydei had teased her about fueling the “competition.” It was all in good fun though. 

“Professor Anaxa is particular to the point of madness,” she was saying. “Yesterday, he made me rewrite an entire section because he didn’t like my word choice on a single line . A single line, Mydei! Can you believe it?” 

Mydei smirked. “I thought you enjoyed a challenge.”

“Perhaps,” she admitted. “But you know who you should never challenge? Cipher. She kept me up all night—” Castorice flushed slightly. “—...proofreading.”

“Uh-huh,” Mydei chuckled, side-eyeing her. “Proofreading.”

They rounded the corner into a quieter street, the sound of the crowd dimming. Mydei was about to tease her further when his steps faltered. A familiar figure stood the near a stall selling old books, browsing the display. Light hair, posture he knew without question, even after all this time. 

The man turned at the sound of their approach, eyes sweeping over Castorice before landing on him. 

“Mydeimos…?” Phainon’s voice cut through the space between them, and for a moment, Mydei could only stand there, the rest of the world narrowing to the sound of this man saying his name.

“You’re pregnant.”

The words were still echoing in his mind long after he’d left the clinic. They’d repeated themselves so many times that they no longer sounded real. He was lying on the couch, staring up at the ceiling, a gentle hand resting on his stomach. The pamphlet the doctor had given him still sat on the coffee table. 

The apartment was still half-finished, the faint smell of fresh paint lingering in the air and construction dust still in the corners. The bakery downstairs was a work in progress with bare counters, unopened crates, just the hum of potential waiting for him to bring it to life. But now, there was even more to think about. 

He’d gone to the clinic on a whim (mostly because Castorice had forced him to). He thought it was nothing, maybe a cold, maybe exhaustion from endless planning paperwork, and late nights sketching out interior design. He’d convinced himself that the nausea, the fatigue, the dizzy spells were just stress-related. He expected to be sent home with painkillers not baby pamphlets and even more decisions to make. 

Pregnant. Eight weeks. The number felt foreign in his mind, disconnected from the days that had passed. Eight weeks ago had been a different life entirely: a warm night, stolen hours, quiet moments where the outside world didn’t matter. The memories were always there and every one of them led back to the same man. 

The doctor had talked about options, whether or not he wanted to go through with it, about timelines and plans, but Mydei wasn’t listening. Not really. All he could really think about was the truth beneath it all. This child—this new life—was his and Phainon’s .

He stared down at his hands, fingers curling into the fabric of his hoodie. Whatever he was working towards and had imagined for himself was changing. He squeezed his eyes shut, grabbing one of his throw pillows and groaned into it to muffle the sound. 

Was he really going to have a baby?

☼

It was late afternoon when he was sitting at the library with Castorice and Cipher, the table littered with half-empty cups and books. Castorice was describing a long day in class, her hands wrapped around a cup as if to warm them. Cipher sat back in her chair, tossing in the occasional dry remark that made Castorice shake her head with a small, amused smile. 

“Mydei… you’ve been quiet today,” Castorice said gently tilting her head toward him. “Quieter than usual.”

Cipher glanced at him too, brows lifting. “Something’s on your mind. C’mon, spit it out.”

“M’fine,” Mydei mumbled, but his voice lacked any real conviction. 

“Mm,” Castorice replied, unconvinced. “You don’t have to tell us if you don’t want to, but we’re here for you.”

“Buuut if you don’t tell us, it might just eat you alive,” Cipher added unhelpfully, earning her a look from Castorice. 

The tightness in his chest had been building for a while now, through every sleepless night, every quiet moment where he imagined what telling Phainon would do. He thought about how Phainon was chasing his dreams without the thought of something permanent tying him down. If Mydei wasn’t enough to make him stay, a baby would just be a burden, wouldn’t it?

They were friends. He’d kept in touch with Phainon for the first few weeks but between timezones and schedules, eventually the messages slowed and Mydei only caught glimpses of Phainon’s new life through the photos he posted. 

He swallowed, downing the rest of his drink, and before he could stop himself, the words slipped out. 

“I’m pregnant.” 

Silence stretched over the table. Castorice’s eyes widened, though her voice stayed soft when she reached out to place a hand atop his and asked, “How far along?” 

“About… eight weeks when I found out. Longer now.” 

Cipher leaned forward slightly, her expressions a mix of shock and calculation. “Do you want to…?”

Mydei sighed and smiled just slightly. “Yeah… I think so.” 

☼

It was late. The apartment was quiet except for the faint hum of the fridge. Mydei was in bed, phone in hand, the glow casting shadows on the ceiling. His thumb hovered over Phainon’s contact. 

He typed out a message: We need to talk. Deleted it. Tried again: I found out something, it’s important. No, that was too vague. I’m pregnant. Too blunt. Why was this so difficult? Every message just felt wrong. There was no easy way to do this, and maybe, just maybe, a part of him didn’t want to upend Phainon’s life this way. 

He set his phone down on the nightstand, turning onto his side and adjusting his pillow. His hand found its way to his stomach. He closed his eyes and in the stillness that followed, a quiet decision was made. 

This child would be his to raise. 

☼

Mydei stood in the small, sunlit room that would soon be his daughter’s nursery. The walls were half-painted in a muted sage green, the soft colour catching the afternoon light. A half-assembled crib leaned against one wall, the instructions folded neatly on the dresser beside a stack of unopened baby clothes. 

He’d thought of this room as a guest room when he’d moved in, but fate had other plans. Maybe it was always meant to be hers. 

His phone buzzed from the windowsill, the family groupchat lighting up. 

Mother

Have you picked up that lavender oil yet?

It helped me in sleep in the last months

Father

And you’re not carrying those boxes 

up the stairs by yourself, are you now?

Mydei huffed softly, typing back:

Yes, Mother

and Father, I’m not fragile.  

His mother and father had been supportive since the day they’d found out over Friday night dinner, but in the quiet moments, Mydei knew they had questions. 

When are you going to tell him?

Are you going to tell him?

Why haven’t you told him?

Mydei shook off the thoughts, setting his phone down again and glancing over at the rocking chair in the corner. The cushions were still wrapped in plastic, but he could already pictured sitting there with her. As he bent down to pick up another piece of the crib, a flutter of movement inside him made him pause, his hand instinctively settling over his stomach. 

“Hey, little one,” he murmured, his voice low, almost shy. “Excited, hm?”

“Talking to yourself again, huh?” Cipher’s voice rang out with amusement as she leaned against the doorframe with a hand on her hip, her gaze flicking to the paint cans and the half-finished crib. “I thought I was supposed to help with this stuff.”

Mydei smiled faintly, brushing off his hands. “I’m perfectly capable of setting up a nursery.”

☼

Mydei walked slowly along the narrow cobblestone street, a canvas bag slung over one shoulder. The late morning sun warmed his back and distracted from the flutters just below his ribs. He’d picked up a few essentials from the farmer’s market: some eggs, herbs, a loaf of sourdough, but also a jar of honey and some pastries just because the craving had struck. 

As he passed by a small park, the sound of children’s laughter drew his attention. A boy, probably no more than five years old, stood alone. His hands twisted into the hem of his shirt, his wide eyes scanning the crowd and apparent worry beginning to cloud his face. 

“Are you alright?” Mydei asked gently, slowing his steps. 

The boy shook his head. “I can’t find mama.”

Mydei gave him a reassuring smile, kneeling with a hand on his stomach. “How about we look together. Do you remember what she’s wearing?”

“A red coat,” he replied quickly. 

They walked slowly along the park’s edge, but Mydei didn’t miss the way the boy kept glancing over at his stomach. He kept his voice light as he spoke. “You know, I’m going to have a baby soon too.”

The boy’s face lit up with curiosity. “A boy or a girl?!”

“A girl,” Mydei said, smiling faintly. “She’s not here yet, but she likes to make her presence known.”

“Will she play in the park?” he asked. 

“When she’s older,” Mydei chuckled. “I think she’ll like it.”

Mydei continued to scan the crowd for the boy’s mother as they walked alongside each other. Within minutes, a woman in a red coat came hurrying toward them, relief crossing her features. She knelt to embrace the boy, thanking Mydei over and over again. 

“It’s no problem, really,” Mydei said in parting, watching them walk away hand in hand. 

The faintest smile tugged at his lips on the way home. The warmth in his chest lingering, a reminder of the life growing inside him and the quiet promise that he’d always keep her safe. 

☼

The scent of cinnamon and cardamon filled the air. It was a busy morning at the bakery and Mydei had been up all morning, rolling out dough and portioning out fillings. Now, the sun was at its peak and the windows were cracked open to let in the cool summer breeze as the little shop bustled with life.

Mydei moved with his usual efficiency, a damp cloth in one hand as he wiped down the counter between orders. He’d gotten used to the routine even through the pregnancy. He’d had help, of course, from his parents and friends to make sure he didn't overwork himself. Contrary to popular belief, he did take some days off when things got a little too overwhelming.  

“You really shouldn’t be on your feet so much,” an older woman said with a click of her tongue. Mydei looked up at her. She was seated at a nearby table with a cappuccino in front of her. “If I were you, I’d be making my husband do all the heavy lifting.” There was a teasing tone in her voice. 

Mydei offered a smile, tucking a loose strand of hair behind his ear. “It’s not so bad,” he murmured. 

“You say that now~,” she gave him a pointed look before sipping her coffee. 

No one ever asked directly, not really, but the assumption was always there. That someone else was in the picture. That there was another half at home waiting for him close up, who had dinner on the table, who held him at night, and who would be there when their daughter came.  

Mydei always let the comments slide. It was no one’s business but his own. 

“I’ll slow down when she tells me to,” he responded softly. 

“Ah, a girl!” the woman beamed. “How lovely. Does she kick much?”

“All the time,” Mydei huffed a small laugh. “Usually right before I’m about to sleep.”

“Well, that’s a good sign. She’s got spirit.”

Mydei glanced down for a moment, his hand drifting unconsciously toward the swell beneath his apron. It was second nature at this point. Yeah , he thought. She’s definitely got spirit just like—

Her father. Just like Phainon.

After the last customer drifted out with a box of croissants, the shop quieted. Mydei leaned against the counter and exhaled slowly, stretching his lower back with one hand while the other rested over his belly. She shifted beneath his palm. It was stronger and sharper than before. 

He stilled. Waited. Then he felt it again. 

Not just a flutter this time. 

“Oh,” he breathed. 

He straightened slowly, blinking at the kitchen clock overhead and taking in deep breaths. 

There was a lull. Then another wave. 

It was time to meet her.

Mydei froze. 

Phainon was standing just ahead of him, looking at him with that same smile and soft eyes that made his knees feel a little weak. He looked older, though not in a bad way. His hair was a little longer and his features sharper, but he was still Phainon. Still the same man that had left years ago. Still Augusta's father. 

He didn’t realize he hadn’t said anything until Castorice’s voice cut in. 

“Phainon,” she said softly. Casually. A little too casual for what was unraveling. 

Mydei’s gaze didn't waver, even as his stomach churned. He knew this was a possibility with Phainon back after all. He’d braced for it. 

And yet…

It still felt like the air had been knocked out of him. 

“I hope I’m not interrupting,” Phainon spoke up

Castorice shook her head with a small chuckle. “Perfect timing actually,” she began. “Mydei and I were just about to grab lunch, you should join us.”

Mydei opened his mouth as if to object, but Castorice didn’t give him the chance. Her hand went lightly to Phainon’s arm like the decision had already been made. “There’s a little bistro just down the block. You remember it, don’t you?”

Phainon nodded. “Of course.” He still hadn’t looked away from Mydei. 

“Perfect,” Castorice clapped her hands together. 

The walk to the bistro was quiet. Castorice led the conversation with practiced ease while Mydei gave short answers and Phainon seemed content to just listen. Still, Mydei couldn’t shake the feeling that she was planning something. 

It wasn’t until they were seated that Casotrice glanced down at her phone with a theatrical frown.

“Ah—Professor Anaxa is waiting on me for something,” she said, already gathering her things. “It completely slipped my mind. You two catch up.” 

Mydei glared at her as she walked out while mouthing talk to him with a pointed look. Mydei sighed, letting out a small groan. 

“Something tells me you’re not happy to see me,” Phainon began. “That or—you don’t like the food.”

“The food’s fine,” Mydei offered simply, taking a bite as if to make a point. 

“You didn’t text.”

“Neither did you.”

“I wasn’t…I wasn’t sure if you wanted me to,” Phainon admitted, poking at his salad. “After everything that happened. That night we…” he trailed off for a moment. “I was afraid everything had changed. And then as time passed, it just got harder. I kept thinking you might’ve moved on. That you probably had someone in your life now, someone better.”

“Neither was I. You had—have a new life,” Mydei responded, glancing over at a nearby couple with their child. How could he have kept in touch when he was harbouring a life-changing secret?  

Phainon tilted his head, letting out a low chuckle that made Mydei’s heart ache. “Seems like we’ve been going around in circles,” he said fondly. “How about this? I take full responsibility this time . But—” he waved around his fork. “—Next time, it’s your turn.” 

“I suppose that’s fair enough.” 

Phainon smiled. Mydei swallowed, his throat tight. Everything was unraveling. Things he’d spent years tucking away. But here they were. And his smile. God, it looked so much like hers. 

He shifted in his seat, “You still ramble when you’re nervous.” 

Phainon laughed, sheepish. “Only around certain people.”

Mydei’s gaze softened, just slightly. Not guarded like the way he’d come into this. No longer cold. A little… tired. And maybe, underneath it all, still aching. 

“Hyacine mentioned that you opened the bakery. How’s business?”

“Steady. And the university?”

Phainon groaned a little. “Busy. Aglaea has me buried in books, but… it’s fulfilling. Hey—maybe I’ll stop by to get my next caffeine fix from you,” he said, leaning forward on his elbows. 

Mydei blinked. “Careful. I might just make you pay extra.” 

The check came not long after, and Phainon didn’t hesitate to reach for it. Mydei opened his mouth, but Phainon cut in before he could protest. 

“I’ve got it. Let me.”

Mydei didn’t argue. Maybe it was easier this way. 

They stepped out into the sunlit street. The breeze had picked up, tugging gently at the edges of Mydei’s coat. He glanced at the sky, then at his phone. 

His stomach dropped. 

“ Shit, shit, shit,” he muttered. “I’m late.”

Phainon turned, brows raised. “Late?” 

Mydei was already stepping off the curb. “I’ve got to go.” 

Phainon looked like he wanted to ask more, but Mydei didn’t give him the chance before he was gone. 

☼

Steam clung to the bathroom mirror as Mydei sat on the small wooden stool beside the bathtub, sleeves rolled to the elbow. Augusta sat in the tub, happily squeezing a rubber ducky as foam gathered around her shoulders. 

Mydei reached for the shampoo bottle, squirting some into his hand before gently massaging it through her curls. 

His mind was elsewhere, still caught on the unexpected lunch a few days ago, on things Phainon had said. The what-ifs. What could’ve been. 

He murmured a soft acknowledgment to Augusta recounting her day. He grabbed the handheld, but his hand fumbled and in the next motion, he turned it on without checking the temperature. 

A burst of cold water shot out and splashed across her back. 

Augusta shrieked. “Mama!”

Mydei snapped his attention back. He twisted the handle until the warmth returned, testing it with two fingers before beginning to wash the shampoo out. 

“Sorry, princess. Is that better?”

She nodded with a shiver, bottom lip jutting out slightly. “You weren’t looking.” 

“I know,” he said, brushing curls away from her forehead. “Mama was distracted.” 

“Were you thinking about work?”

He hesitated. “Something like that.”

She was silent for a moment as if she was taking it all in, but that answer seemed to satisfy her enough. Once clean, Mydei wrapped her towel around her and lifted her out of the bath, letting her make her way into her room. 

After helping her into her pajamas, she made a little leap into her bed before grabbing her favourite plush lion. He settled in beside her, letting her curl into his side, just below his chin. He opened the storybook she loved. 

Halfway through the story, she yawned, eyelids already drooping. Mydei adjusted the blanket around her and finished the last few lines in a quieter tone. He closed the book and leaned in to kiss her forehead. 

“Night, babygirl.”

“Night-night, mama,” she mumbled sleepily. 

Mydei stayed there for a moment, making sure she was actually asleep. Then he stood, flicked off the light, and stepped quietly out into the hallway. 

He padded to his own room, pulling off his shirt and settling into the bed. There was so much changing around them and so many truths he needed to tell. But Augusta was warm and safe. 

And for now, he tried not to let the guilt eat at him. 

☼

Mydei was just finishing up vacuuming the carpet when the knock at the door sounded. He unplugged the appliance, letting it lean against the wall before heading to open the door. He expected to find his parents on the other side with Augusta. They’d offered to watch her for the afternoon to spend time with her, and give Mydei a little break. Instead—

“Hey,” Castorice raised her hand in a small wave. “Got a sec?” 

Mydei nodded, stepping aside to let her in. 

“Augusta isn’t home, is she?”

“Mother and father took her out,” Mydei glanced over at the clock. “They should be back.” 

“Mm,” Castorice hummed in response, placing a small bag of scones she knew Mydei liked onto the counter. “I won’t be too long. I just wanted to talk before things got too hectic.”

He raised an eyebrow. 

Castorice folded her arms. “Cipher and I have been talking about the wedding again.”

“Don’t tell me you’re changing the venue again,” he teased. 

Castorice. “No, not,” she waved her hands. “It’s about the guest list.”

Mydei didn’t say anything. 

“We want you there, obviously,” she said. “And Augusta.” 

He leaned back against the sink, bracing himself. 

“But,” she continued, voice gentler now, “we want to invite Phainon.”

Mydei let out a small sigh. “I figured.”

“I know it’s a lot,” she added. “And I promise we haven’t said anything to him yet. I just… I thought you deserved a heads-up. Because we’d really love for both of you to be there, and we’d never want it to be uncomfortable for you.”

Mydei looked down at his hands. 

“Mydei…” she said softly, placing a hand on his arm. “You’ve been raising her on your own for so long, and I know you're perfectly capable. But, I think… it’s time to tell him. He deserves to know before things get even more complicated. Telling him won't erase what you've done for her either.”

Mydei met her gaze. “You always did have awful timing.”

She smiled. “You’re lucky I didn’t send Cipher.” 

They stood in silence for a beat before Mydei walked her to the door. She paused at the threshold and looked at him once more. 

“She looks like you, you know,” she said softly. “But she’s got his heart.” 

“What if he hates me?” 

Castorice shook her head. “I think we both know that could never be true.”

Then she was gone. 

And Mydei stood there in the quiet, letting the words sink in. The door was still open when he heard little footsteps running upstairs. 

“Mama, I’m home!” 

“Slow down, little star!” Eurypon’s voice echoed from down the hall as Augusta came barreling into him. Mydei scooped her up with ease, kissing her cheek. 

“Did you have fun with grandma and grandpa?” 

“Mm!” she nodded, resting her head against his shoulder. Then in a hushed tone she whispered, “But I missed Mama.” 

☼

The sky was still dim outside the kitchen window, the first threads of light streaking across rooftops. Mydei moved quickly in the kitchen, tucking in a sandwich and sliced up fruit into his daughter’s lunchbox. He glanced at the clock, there was just enough time to finish his coffee before waking her up. 

Except he didn’t need to. 

Small feet shuffled into the room. Augusta stood in the doorway with a small pout on her face and her hair a little unruly. 

“Mamaaa,” she whined, voice small. “My tummy hurts.” 

Mydei arched a brow. “Does it now?”

She nodded, wrapping her arms around her middle. “It really, really does.”

He gave her a look. It was half skeptical and half amused as he leaned against the count. “Hmm… I didn’t hear any complaints about tummy aches when someone wanted pancakes for dinner.” 

Augusta’s bottom lip jutted out. “It started when I woke up.” 

“Mhmm.” He crossed his arms, crouching down to her level. “No fever?”

“No…”

“No cough?”

“No.”

“How about breakfast?”

“...Maybe bread.” 

He tried to hold firm for a moment long, but then he caved. 

“Alright, alright,” he muttered, scooping her up and carrying her to the couch. He tucked a throw blanket around her. “Toast?”

“With jam, please.”

He shook his head, but he was smiling as he headed back to the kitchen. 

☼

Augusta’s stomach ache had magically cured itself shortly after he’d reported her absence to the school. Mydei had already made a mental note to ask her exactly why she wanted to stay home, but for now, he was content to let her have her way. Especially since, soon enough, things were going to change in ways he wasn’t sure how he’d explain. 

She had been colouring at one of the tables before everything had started to frustrate her, and Mydei knew what that meant. So, he’d sent her into his little office in the back to nap. She had been up since dawn after all. 

Now, the colouring book sat abandoned, opened to page with a half coloured scene and some scribbles. 

Mydei was wiping down the counter when the bell above the door chimed. He looked up. Blinked. Blinked again. 

“Mydei,” Phainon grinned. 

“Phainon…” 

“I thought I’d stop by for that coffee,” he said, amusement in his tone. He continued to rattle off about the place. How it was nice. How he didn’t expect anything less from him. How Mydei never did anything halfway. 

Mydei glanced over at the door of the office. Augusta was asleep in there. Just a couple of feet away. Surely Phainon would be gone before she woke up.

He’d already made up his mind. He was going to tell Phainon, but not like this. They were supposed to meet somewhere quiet—somewhere Mydei could explain gently. 

She wouldn’t wake up. It would be fine.

Mydei gave Phainon a smile as he got to work on making his coffee. 

“I’ve been thinking…” Phainon began. “There’s this show playing next week. Aglaea gave me two tickets,” he said, digging into his messenger bag to hold them up. “You should come with. It’s next Saturday.”

“Ah…I’m usually busy on weekends,” Mydei responded sheepishly, trying to hide the fact that pinpricks of heat were spreading across his face. Did Phainon really just ask him out on a date?

“It’s in the evening if it’s about work.” 

“No, it’s—” 

Mydei’s voice was cut off by the sound of small footsteps, padding out of the little office tucked away in the corner. Augusta appeared behind the counter, rubbing one eye with her fist. 

“Mama, I’m hungry.” 

Fuck.

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.html:
The world had slowed to that moment. The words escaped from his—their daughter’s mouth. She was still standing behind the counter, oblivious to shift in the air. 

Mydei’s gaze was locked with Phainon’s, and the silence between them rang louder than any chime. The espresso shot Mydei had pulled was spilled across the floor, the small ceramic cup rolling against the base of the counter with a hollow clink. He didn’t even remember letting it go. He couldn’t think about anything else. Not when Phainon was standing there. Not when Augusta had said “Mama” so naturally. 

Phainon hadn’t reacted at first. He just stood there like he was trying to process the moment. The question was there behind his eyes, but he didn’t need to ask. The truth was something they both knew. 

Augusta let out a little gasp, grabbing the mop leaning against the back wall and dragging it over to him with a determined little grunt. Mydei snapped his attention to her. Right . She was still here. She didn’t understand what she’d just unraveled. 

She hoisted herself onto the stool by the counter, leaning over on her elbows. “Don’t worry mister!” she chirped. “Mama isn’t always clumsy.” She added, completely oblivious to the fact that this man was her father and looking up at him with the kind of innocence only a child could possess. 

She didn’t deserve this. She didn’t deserve to be tangled up in this mess that Mydei created. 

He turned toward her. 

“Go wash up, sweetheart,” Mydei nudged her back lightly, managing to keep his voice steady. “I’ll heat up your lunch,” he added with a softness only reserved for her. 

“Okay!” She chirped, already bouncing off to the bathroom. 

Mydei waited until she was gone before turning back to Phainon. The cheerful demeanour he had come in with was no longer there, replaced only by what Mydei could discern as betrayal behind his eyes. 

Please don’t look at me like that.

“Mydei you…” Phainon’s voice faltered, cracking at the edges. He exhaled sharply and dragged a hand down his face. “You never thought to tell me?”

“I was going to tell you,” Mydei said quickly. “This wasn’t the plan. It wasn’t supposed to be like this.”

“Oh, you had a plan, ” Phainon muttered bitterly. “Was part of the plan keeping this from me for what? Five years? To let me sit across from you like nothing had changed, to let me walk in here while she was sleeping right there?”

Mydei flinched. “It wasn’t like that.”

Phainon shook his head, backing away, hand already gripping the strap of his bag. “I can’t—I don’t even know what to say to you right now.” 

“Phainon.”

But he was already halfway to the door, shoving it open with a sharp push. Mydei followed him out without sparing a second thought, barely registering the bell or the confused glance from the patron who had just entered. 

He caught up to him just past the awning, grabbing his sleeve. 

“Phainon, wait. Please.” A plea. 

Phainon yanked his arm back but stopped, whirling around to face him, hurt and betrayal written across his features. “You lied to me.” 

“I didn’t lie,” Mydei snapped, a bit too defensively. “I just…I kept it to myself.”

“That isn’t any better!” Phainon said, voice rising. 

Mydei’s chest tightened. “You left. I didn’t even know if you were coming back.”

“That didn’t give you the right to keep her from me!”

Mydei swallowed hard, his hands trembling a little. And then it came out, sudden, a little too honest:

“She was all I had left of you!”

Phainon’s expression froze. 

“I couldn’t…I didn’t know if I could bear the thought of not having her,” Mydei continued, voice breaking. “I wasn’t enough to make you stay, but she…she was a piece of you that I got to keep. And time kept slipping away and I—” His throat caught. 

The street around them had quieted. Glances and whispers thrown their way as people passed by the bakery, watching the scene unfold. 

“It wasn’t a punishment,” Mydei whispered. 

Phainon said nothing, his expression unreadable. The hurt was still etched on his face. So was the disbelief. But there was something else beneath it. Something fragile. 

Finally, he looked away. 

“I can’t do this right now,” he said, already walking off. 

This time, Mydei let him. 

The bell above the door jingled again as Augusta pushed the door open with both hands, her eyes wide as she looked up at him with confusion. “Mama? Why did you go outside?” 

Mydei blinked, then quickly turned and knelt down in front of her, brushing his palms against his apron. He tried for a smile, but it didn’t quite reach his eyes. 

“It’s nothing,” he said gently, tucking a strand of hair behind her ear. “I was just helping someone.”

Before she could ask anything further, Mydei leaned in to press a kiss to her temple. “Let’s get your lunch ready,” he murmured. 

☼

The living room was quiet, save for the occasional thump or rustle from Augusta’s room down the hall. She was playing with her blocks. He could hear her narrating something to herself softly, voice rising and falling. 

Mydei was sprawled on the couch, arm thrown across his face while his phone sat facedown on the coffee table, untouched. No new notifications. At least not one he wanted to see. 

“You’re spiraling,” Cipher said in a sing-song voice, stretching her back against the couch from her spot on the floor. She and Castorice had come over earlier in the evening to keep him company once they’d figured out what had happened. How messy everything had gotten. 

“You texted him again, didn’t you?” Castorice asked from her spot on the armchair across from him, her arms wrapped around the throw pillow she’d pulled into her lap. 

Mydei didn’t look at her. “He hasn’t read any of them,” he murmured. “I didn’t expect a response…but I thought he’d at least read them,” he added as he sat up. 

Cipher sighed, pushing herself up on the couch. “You did drop a bomb on him, Mydei.” 

“I know,” Mydei said. “I know I should’ve told him, I know I handled it all wrong, but—” He rubbed his face, pushing back his hair. “I just wanted to do something right.” 

Castorice moved to sit beside him, shoulder nudging his.

“I keep thinking about the look on his face.” Mydei’s voice was raw. “He’s never looked at me like that. Then he just…left.”

“It was just shock,” Cipher offered, more gently this time. “I know I wouldn’t react with perfect grace if I found out I had a kid I never knew about.” 

Castorice nodded. “He just needs time to process.” 

Mydei leaned back, letting his head rest against the back of the couch, throat tight. “What if he never comes back?” 

Cipher flicked his forehead with two fingers. “Stop that,” she said flatly. “Yeah, you kept a secret. Yeah, you meant to tell him. And now he knows. Was it perfect? Of course not. But it’s out there. You two can deal with it like adults and then do whatever dramatic post-fight nonsense you want. I don’t know… make up sex or just glare at each other across the kitchen.” she finished, already checking her nails like she was bored. As if Mydei’s life didn’t implode in a single afternoon. 

Mydei opened his mouth and then closed it again, unsure of what to say to that . Castorice flushed immediately, not meeting his gaze as she muttered something about filters and children being around , elbowing her fiancée. 

From the hallway, Augusta called out. “Mama, look! I made a tower as tall as me!” 

Mydei pushed off the couch to follow the sound of her voice. 

He missed when things were simpler. 

☼

The last of the customers had trickled out about a half an hour ago, leaving just Mydei and Augusta with the scent of coffee and sugar in the air. Mydei stood at the sink, apron still around his waist and his sleeves rolled up to his elbows, up to his wrists in suds. Augusta was balanced on a wooden stool next to him with a small cloth in hand, drying each dish with focus that made his chest ache.

Her little brow furrowed, lips parted slightly in concentration as she turned a clean cup over in the towel. 

Mydei watched her for a moment with fondness before flicking a few water droplets in her direction. 

“Mamaa!” she shrieked, holding up the cloth like a little shield. 

“Can’t help it when you’re so cute,” he replied, reaching over to tickle her side. She giggled, barely keeping her balance but Mydei had an arm around her. 

“Stop!” she laughed breathlessly, trying to squirm away. “I’m working!”

“You’re doing great, the best little helper I could ask for,” he said, tugging her into a hug and kissing the top of her head. She let out a little satisfied hum before she went back to drying the tray in front of her. 

Before either of them could say anything, the bell above the door chimed.

Mydei didn’t look up at first. “I’m sorry, we’re closed for to—” his voice cut off when he saw who had walked in. He was dressed casually, looking a lot more tired than the last time Mydei had seen him. That was expected though. He did learn that he had a daughter after all. His eyes were a little puffy as if he’d been crying and the thought made Mydei’s stomach churn. 

“Phainon…” Mydei’s voice was barely above a whisper.

“Pienon,” Augusta repeated, hand reaching up to tug gently on Mydei’s apron. He gave her a little smile. 

“You know you’ve been such a good helper today, but mama has to talk to mister Phainon,” He explained gently. “Why don’t you go upstairs and get ready for bed, hm?” 

“But I’m not tired,” she frowned. 

“I know, princess,” he nodded. “But it’s a really important talk.”

She pouted, sticking out her bottom lip. “Can I stay?” she asked, looking up at him with pleading eyes. “I’ll be really, really quiet,” she whispered. 

Mydei let out a small sigh. “It's just for grown-ups,” he murmured. “Go brush your teeth, okay? I’ll come up and tuck you in.”

She gave Phainon a curious glance, then back at Mydei, clearly not satisfied but knowing she wasn’t going to get her way this time. With a sigh, she mumbled, “Okay…” and dragged her feet as she disappeared toward the stairs. She shot one last glance at them before she made her way upstairs. 

Mydei waited until he heard the door upstairs click shut before he turned to Phainon. He untied his apron, leaving it on the rack and coming around the counter so they could sit at one of the tables together. 

“She gets curious,” Mydei said quietly, unsure of what exactly came next. “I texted…” he added softly. 

The air between them shifted again. 

“I know,” Phainon responded. He didn’t seem angry anymore, at least not the way he was that day. Maybe disappointed, but not angry. Mydei could live with that. 

“I’m sorry. I really am, Phainon,” Mydei began. “I let my feelings get in the way of what you deserved to know. I know that.”

Phainon let out a little sigh, a little defeated as he slumped back in his chair. “Did you really not think about telling me in these past five years? Did you not…trust me?”

“No, God no, it wasn’t like that… I thought about it all the time. What it would feel like. What you would say. If we would be tog—” Mydei swallowed, voice catching in his throat as he blinked back tears. “You were pursuing what you loved, and I didn’t want to hold you back.” 

Mydei didn’t look at him, but Phainon reached across the table to place a hand atop his. “I wouldn’t have thought about it like that, we could’ve built a life together,” his voice was soft as Mydei inhaled shakily. 

“And now?” Mydei asked futilely, already knowing what the answer would be. Those bridges had been burned long ago. 

Phainon blinked as if he hadn’t expected him to ask. “I don’t know,” he said, not meeting Mydei’s gaze.

A moment of silence passed between them as they let the truth sink in. Phainon retracted his hand and Mydei could only miss the warmth.

Phainon was the first to break the silence. “What’s her name?”

“Augusta.” 

“It’s pretty, it suits her,” he smiled a little fondly. “And she’s four?”

Mydei nodded, hating the way that smile made his heart flutter even if it wasn't meant for him. 

“I want to be in her life. I don’t know if I… if I forgive you but she deserves to have both her parents. I'm not angry, Mydei. I want us to figure this out."

He knew forgiveness wasn’t going to come easy. Mydei knew that, but it didn’t mean that it didn’t hurt any less. Still, even if he had done irreparable damage to his and Phainon’s relationship, he’d do anything for their daughter. And that’s what mattered most. 

“Okay, we’ll figure it out.”

Mydei sat cross legged on the rug, back against the couch as little fingers tugged and twisted sections of his hair. Augusta was sitting on the couch behind him, her tongue poking out in concentration as she worked on a crooked braid. 

He winced slightly when she pulled a little too tightly. “Careful, sweetheart,” he murmured, reaching up to steady the part she’d already done. “I still need that part of my scalp.”

“Sorry mama,” she said, adjusting her fingers. Her brows furrowed. “You moved.” 

He chuckled under his breath and lifted the small hand mirror he’d set beside him earlier, tilting it to get a better look at his little girl’s handiwork. “You’re getting better at this,” he said honestly. 

“Really?!” her voice already lighting up, and she leaned forward slightly to peer at his face. 

“Mhmm.” He nodded. You only tied one of them into a knot,”

She giggled in response before tying off the braid with a small red band. Mydei caught her reflection in the mirror and his heart squeezed at her tiny proud smile. 

He tilted his head, glancing up at her. “Alright, come here for a sec.” 

Augusta blinked. “Why?”

“We need to talk”

Her expression shifted almost immediately. “It wasn’t me, mama!” she said quickly. A little too quickly. 

Mydei turned toward the couch and gave her a long, narrow-eyed look. “Mm. I don’t recall accusing you of anything yet.”

Her eyes widened as she clapped her hands over her mouth. “Oops.”

“You’re not in trouble,” he said, easing himself up beside her and tapping her knee, “but we are circling back to that later.”

She sighed dramatically, swinging her legs back and forth. “Then what’s it about?”

“It’s about Mister Phainon.”

That got her attention. 

Augusta gasped, clasping her hands together in her lap. “Mister Phainon is so fun! He always reads stories in the best voices, and he showed me another way to tie my shoes that’s way faster than bunny ears, and he even let me have two candies! Even though you said only one…” she added quickly, eyes darting to Mydei guiltily like maybe if she said it fast enough, he wouldn't notice. 

Mydei gave her a flat look. “We’ll circle back to that too.”

She bit back a smile, chin tipping toward her knees. 

He exhaled through his nose and gently pulled her into his lap, settling her sideways so her back was against his arm. 

It had been around six weeks since that night in the bakery when everything had been laid bare between him and Phainon. Since then, things had shifted cautiously. Phainon had been around more often. He’d been spending more time with Augusta. 

He came over to the bakery in the evenings after work occasionally to keep Augusta company or he’d join them at the park to push her on the swings and catch her at the end of the slide—just little ways they could connect.

But he hadn’t said anything. At least not about who he was exactly to her. 

He and Mydei had agreed that they’d take things slow. 

Mydei had thought that what was broken between him and Phainon was mending itself when the three of them were together, but then, Phainon would leave with a smile and wave meant just for Augusta, and Mydei would feel the old ache beneath his ribs again. 

“You know how sometimes it takes grown-ups a while to figure things out?” Mydei began.

“Like when you take soooo long deciding what to make for dinner?” She offered.

He huffed a small laugh. “Something like that.”

Augusta leaned into his chest, still listening but clearly a little sleepy—though she would never admit that. 

“There’s something important I want to tell you,” he said, voice quieter. “About Mister Phainon.”

She nodded. 

“You know how grandpa and grandma are my mother and father?” 

“Uh-huh, you always say,” Augusta said, dropping her voice down an octave before adding: “Mother, Father.”

Mydei just shook his head fondly. “Well…just like that, Mister Phainon is your father.”

Mydei braced himself for the onslaught of questions, but only silence followed. Augusta pulled back, a finger to her lips. She glances up at him and then down at her knees, then back again.  

“It’s okay if you’re confused, you can ask me anything,” he reassured her, brushing her hair back from her eyes. 

She was quiet for a moment longer, then asked: “Do I have to call him papa?” 

“Only if you want,” he said. “You can ask him.” 

Another pause.

“Where was he?” 

“He had some… really important work to do, but he’s back now,” Mydei answered carefully.

She looked up at him this time, eyes glassy. “Does that mean I have to live with him?” 

“No, sweetheart,” he said, pulling her closer immediately. “You’ll still be here with me. But sometimes, if you want, you might visit him. He’ll read you your bedtime stories, or pick you up from school.” 

Augusta's lip trembled. “But I like when you do those things, mama.” She buried her face in his chest. “I don’t wanna go away.”

Mydei’s throat tightened. He held her close, one hand cradling the back of her head “Oh, baby. You’re not going anywhere and neither am I. I know things are changing, but you won’t ever have to do anything you don’t want to. We’ll take it one day at a time.” 

She didn’t say anything, but she nodded against his chest. He felt the faint tremble in her shoulder as she sniffled softly. 

He pulled back just enough to wipe her tears with the pads of his thumbs and kiss the tip of her nose. The gesture made her giggle softly. 

“Do you wanna tell me what you definitely didn’t do now?” 

Augusta averted her eyes, twiddling her thumbs. “I gave someone a brownie when you went to the bathroom the other day.”

“Hmm.” Mydei hummed in response. “And what have we said about giving things away that aren’t ours?”

She let out a small sigh, huffing a little. “Not to do it unless it gets mama a husband.”

Mydei blinked. Opened his mouth, then blinked again. What?

“Auntie Cipher is not babysitting you again.”

☼

The morning light had just begun to sift through the curtains when Mydei cracked open Augusta’s bedroom door. She was curled under the cover with a blanket over her and a stuffed lion tucked under one arm. She had insisted on more than one story the night before, and he suspected it was because of what they talked about. 

Mydei smiled as he knelt beside her. He brushed his knuckles along her cheek. “Augusta,” he said softly, thumb brushing a loose curl from her forehead. “Morning, sleepyhead.”

She stirred, eyes fluttering open. “Five more minutes…mama…please.”

“Time to get ready for school,” he murmured. “But,” he paused, smoothing the covers down a little. “If you’re feeling overwhelmed after what we talked about last night, you don’t have to go. You can be my little helper today.”

Augusta blinked up at him, still bleary eyed. Then, after a beat, she shook her head slowly. “I wanna go, it’s my turn for show and tell.”

Oh,” he said, lips twitched into a soft smile. “Important business, then.”

She nodded seriously. “I’m bringing the rock pa—Mister Phainon helped me paint.”

Mydei’s throat caught for a moment, but he just smiled and kissed her forehead. “Then let’s get you dressed before you’re late.”

☼

The bakery was a little slower that morning. An elderly couple sat at one of the tables, chatting over hot drinks and pastries. Some university students had occupied another table, fueled only by caffeine and academic stress. Mydei didn’t mind though, especially since Castorice and Cipher were waiting at one of the tables. 

He set down a trio of small plates on the table, each with a different slice of cake. One was a fresh berry combination, another was white chocolate pistachio, and the third was a fudgy dark chocolate—Cipher’s pick.

Castorice already had her fork in hand. “This one looks amazing,” she said, pointing to the pistachio. “Not that I expected any less.”

“Oh, our little prince has outdone himself~” Cipher licked her lips, fork already diving into the dark chocolate without hesitation.

Mydei pulled the chair across from them, suppressing a smile as he pulled out his notepad. “Alright. Start talking.”

“I might need another slice of this one just to make sure,” Cipher said thoughtfully. 

“You just want an excuse to eat more cake,” Mydei deadpanned. 

“Isn’t that what this is about anyways.”

Castorice laughed softly, nudging Cipher with her shoulder lightly. Cipher gave her a small smile before offering her a bite of her slice. She chewed thoughtfully. “We could do a tier of each… oh uh… if that isn’t too much trouble, De.”

He let out a small sigh, slumping back in his seat. “You two don’t make things easy, you know that right?”

“So that’s a yes,” Cipher said as she licked the frosting off her thumb. “Oh and—invites went out too.”

Castorice grinned, clasping her hands together. “You and Augusta should be getting yours soon.”

“She’s going to be so excited,” he replied, but Castorice’s gaze lingered. 

“...We did invite Phainon too,” she added gently. 

Mydei’s hands didn’t pause over the notepad as he sketched a rough outline of the design, and he didn’t look up either. “I didn’t expect you not to.”

Cipher exchanged a glance with Castorice, then leaned forward slightly. “You’re really okay with that?”

Mydei let out a slow breath and finally looked up at them. “It’s fine. He knows about Augusta and she knows about him.”

Cipher leaned forward on her elbows. “Sooo,” her tone was way too casual to be innocent. “Was it sex or glaring at each other?”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “We talked.”

“Hmm,” Cipher hummed, not buying it. “Talked, huh? So, like talking, then kissing, then talking while kissing.”

Mydei gave her a look, getting up from his seat and smoothing down his apron. “Your appointment is over.”

“Oh come on!” Cipher exclaimed. “I~ wouldn’t judge you for having some fun.”

“She’s just teasing,” Castorice reassured. “I think it’s great you and Phainon are trying to do what’s best for Augusta,” she said, setting her fork down with a clink. She shared a glance with Cipher and a shy smile formed on her lips. “But I hope things get better between the two of you.”

Yeah, Mydei thought, I hope so too.

☼

“Mama!!” Augusta’s voice filtered down the hallway from her room. “I found the yellow overalls! But I need the white shirt.”

Mydei smiled a little to himself as he wiped his hands on a dish towel and headed down the hall. She’d spent the last hour picking out just the right outfit. Phainon was coming over, and this time, she had something important she wanted to ask him. 

Alright, alright,” he murmured as he stepped into her room. “Let’s see what we’ve got.”

She stood barefoot in the middle of the room, sunflower hairpin already clipped in her hair, holding up her overalls in front of the mirror as if she were still deliberating. Mydei crouched by the dresser and rummaged through the neatly folded clothes until he found the white ruffled shirt. 

“Arms up,” he instructed, helping her into it. 

Once she was dressed, she turned to the mirror with serious eyes, smoothing down the front of her overalls. She adjusted the hairpin slightly and then went straight to her box of bracelets. 

“Alright, little one,” Mydei said as he stood and stretched. “I think you’re all set to go.”

Augusta nodded, and then she looked up at him. “Mama.”

“Hm?”

“Can we get another baby?” she asked quietly. 

Mydei paused for a moment. That hadn’t been the question he expected. “What makes you ask that?” He asked softly, crouching back down to her level.

She shrugged. “You said Mister Phainon is my papa and he’s back now, so…can’t you get another baby?”

Mydei chuckled. “That’s not how it works, sweetheart.” 

“Then how does it work?” 

The knock on the door came just in time before he could even think about how to answer that question—merciful timing. 

Augusta lit up, bouncing a little on her feet. “I’ll get it!” 

By the time Mydei followed, the door was already open and Phianon stood just at the threshold. 

“Hey, sunshine—” Phainon started, laughing as she collided with him. “Is that a new hairpin I see?”

“Uh-huh,” she nodded excitedly. “Mama got me a whole box! Wanna see?”

“Of course,” he said, leaning in to kiss her cheek. “But maybe after I say hi to mama?”

“‘Kay!” she chirped, skipping toward her room. 

Phainon stood, brushing lightly past Mydei as their eyes met. 

“She’s been excited all day,” Mydei murmured. 

“I can tell,” his voice was warm. “You look—” He stopped himself. “How…how have you been?”

“Busy,” Mydei said, folding his arms over as he tilted his head. He could’ve sworn Phainon’s eyes followed the movement. “With the little one,” he added fondly.

Their gazes lingered for a beat longer before Augusta returned with the box as promised. Phainon turned toward her and Mydei headed toward the kitchen, glancing once over his shoulder. 

Augusta sat crossed legged on the floor by the window, opening the music box with her hair clips inside. The tune carried into the kitchen.

“These are all the new ones,” she said, holding the box up proudly. “Mama let me pick them out myself.”

“They’re beautiful,” Phainon said, crouching down next to her. “But I think this one’s my favourite.” He pointed to a red flower. 

She smiled, quiet for a second. Her fingers fiddled with one of the bracelets she’d taken off. Mydei knew the question was coming. They’d already talked about it. He stood in the doorway to the living room, giving his daughter an encouraging nod. 

“Hey,” Phainon asked gently. “Is something wrong?”

She hesitated, then shook her head, but she still seemed a little unsure. Mydei crossed the room, moving to sit down beside her. 

Phainon tilted his head. “Something on your mind, then?”

She toyed with a little ruffle on her clothes, glancing up at Mydei. 

“Go ahead, sweetheart.” he encouraged. 

There was a pause. 

Then, almost a whisper: “Can I…Can I call you papa?” 

Phainon froze for a heartbeat. “Oh,” he breathed. Augusta peeked up at him, the corners of her mouth pulled down into a nervous frown like she’d already been prepared for him to say no. 

“Of course you can,” he said softly. “If that’s what you want and if mama’s okay with it.”

Mydei nodded. 

Her shoulders sagged with relief, and a small smile broke through. “Okay,” she replied as Phainon pulled her in for a hug. His eyes were a little glassy when they met Mydei’s as he mouthed a soft ‘ thank you.'

"Papaaa," Augusta giggled. "You’re squishing me."

☼

Mydei stood in the doorway for a moment, watching as Augusta wriggled under the covers, her sunflower hairpin now sitting in the dish on her nightstand beside a drawing she’d done of her and Phainon. The quiet of the evening was settling over them, their home a little quieter now that Phainon had gone home. 

“Lights out in three, babygirl,” he said, crossing the room to tuck the blanket properly over her. 

“Okay,” she mumbled, her eyes already half-closed.

He smoothed her hair back, brushing a stray strand off her cheek before he leaned down to kiss her forehead. As he straightened, something on the floor near the foot of her bed caught his eye—a glint of silver.

He crouched down to pick it up. It was a pendant. Small and oval-shaped, hanging from a chain that was definitely too long for a child. He turned it over in his palm. 

“Where did this come from?” he asked softly. 

Augusta blinked sleepily, rolling onto her side. “Papa let me wear it,” she said, voice barely there. “He forgot it…” her voice trailed off and Mydei didn’t catch the rest except the words "mama" and "pretty"

Mydei’s hand stilled for a second. He looked down at it again, his thumb brushing the clasp before he gently opened it. The hinge gave way with a soft click. 

Inside was a picture faded around the edges. 

A picture of him.

Chapter End Notes
