chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.html:
Mydei had resolved to just not think about it. 

The rain had been going all afternoon, pattering against the windows. Their apartment was quiet save for the low rumble of the washing machine running in the background. 

He told himself it was peaceful. 

It was the kind of evening he should’ve been grateful for. The house was clean (from the mud Augusta had tracked in earlier), dinner was finished, and the laundry was mostly done. Augusta hadn’t even fought him on anything today either. 

So, naturally, Mydei’s resolve was crumbling. 

Nope, he thought, shaking his head as he caught himself staring at the pendant sitting on the far corner of the table. He hadn’t meant to leave it there. He should’ve tucked it away somewhere until Augusta could give it back to him. No, he should’ve forgotten about it entirely. 

Still, he’d opened it a few times since that night to convince himself he was just seeing things. Phainon wouldn’t have kept a picture of him in a pendant he wore all the damn time. 

He wouldn’t 

He wouldn’t 

He wouldn’t 

But… he had. 

Everytime Mydei had unlatched the pendant the photo remained the same. It was still a picture of him from back when they were younger. When they were still dancing the line between friendship and something more. 

But, it wasn’t just the picture either that him thinking this way. It was the fact that Phainon had kept it close to his heart for all this time. 

Nope, nope, nope.

They were co-parents. Friends maybe, but nothing more. They were doing this for Augusta. 

He turned his attention back to the folder in his hands, flipping through some of Augusta’s work that her teacher had sent to be reviewed. Spelling tests, worksheets, a drawing of a lion and a fluffy dog, a few notices. The usual. 

Then a little invitation caught his eye. A small piece of cardstock with gold trim on the edges. 

Spring Showcase - Thursday 7pm 

He furrowed his brow, holding it up as Augusta padded into the kitchen, standing on her toes to grab a box of crackers. “Hey, did you forget something?” he asked, waving the little card around. 

Her eyes lit up immediately. “Oh! That’s for our performance!” 

“A performance, huh? What part are you playing?” 

“It’s a surprise.” She said, bouncing in place a little. “But I’ve been practicing really hard!”

He reached over to pat her head, taking the box of crackers from her hands to hand her two instead. “You’re going to be amazing.”

She grinned, but then paused like she had a question. “Can papa come too?”

Mydei nodded after a beat. “I’ll ask him,” he said. “If he’s free, I’m sure he’d love to.”

He let out a little sigh when she padded back to her room, trying hard not to think about it again. 

☼

Gorgo and Eurypon had come over for the afternoon. Mydei already had tea stepping in cups on the table while he brought out a fruit platter. 

“She really is growing fast,” Gorgo smiled fondly, casting a glance over at her granddaughter playing quietly to herself in the living room. “It feels like just yesterday she was still learning to walk.”

Mydei set the platter down. “Now she tries to stage pillow fights before bedtime.”

Eurypon chuckled. “She gets that from you, no doubt.”

Conversation flowed easily between Mydei and his parents. They talked about business at the bakery, how Augusta was doing in school, and even how Phainon had been coming around more often to spend time with her. Mydei hadn’t thought twice while talking about him and Augusta.  

“So he’s been around more,” Eurypon hummed, reaching for an orange wedge from the plate

Mydei nodded. “He’s been…really good about it. She’s attached to him by the hip whenever he comes over, but I shouldn’t have expected any less. He’s Phainon after all,” he’d said the last part without thinking. 

There was a pause. 

His mother’s eyes flicked up, her expression unreadable as she exchanged a glance with his father. “And how are things?”

Mydei blinked. “I just told you. Augusta really loves him.” 

His mother shook her head, giving him a pointed look, her finger jabbing into his chest. “No, Mydeimos, I was asking about you and Phainon.”

Mydei looked between his parents, then let out a short, incredulous laugh. There was no way they were serious. “There is no me and Phainon. We’re just co-parenting.”

Eurypon raised an eyebrow, unconvinced. “Are you sure that’s all it is?”

“Yes,” Mydei said, maybe a little too quickly. “We’re just figuring out what’s best for Augusta.”

“You love so fiercely,” Gorgo began. “And yet, you can’t spare any for him?”

Mydei looked away, eyes settling on Augusta instead. She was lying on her stomach, a crayon in hand as she kicked her legs in the air. She’d been surprisingly calm this afternoon, but Mydei had chalked it up to focus since she was humming to herself softly. 

“That’s not—” he stopped, jaw tightening. 

He took a breath. 

“I kept her from him for four years,” he said, the words slipping out softer than he’d meant them to be. “I would be a fool to think that there was anything left between us. That he could ever want me."

The room fell silent. 

Gorgo folded her hands on the table, voice gentle as always. “I just think you two should talk about it.”

Mydei looked down at his tea, watching the steam curl upwards. 

“I just want to get things right for her,” he said truthfully. 

“I know you do,” she placed a hand on his shoulder. “But a mistake, however big, shouldn’t stop you from thinking that you deserve to be happy, my son.”

“But no matter what you choose or what happens, we’re always in your corner,” Eurypon added. “We just want what’s best for both of you.”

☼

The day of the performance had arrived, and Augusta looked like she might burst from how long she’d kept the secret. Mydei had actually been impressed with how long she’d gone without even giving him a hint to what their performance was going to be about. 

Mydei noticed her reaching for a cookie from the tray sitting on the cooling rack, catching it just in time. She looked up at him with puppy-dog eyes. 

“You know these are for tonight,” he hummed. 

Augusta frowned, her shoulders slumping a little. Mydei had spent the afternoon scooping out different types of cookies onto trays. Augusta had made a list of flavours that she thought were appropriate and he’d chosen 3 out of the 9 she’d said-snickerdoodle, chocolate chip, and cut-outs with sprinkles. 

The request had come in from the PTA a couple of nights ago in the form of a polite email. He’d catered for school events, and…it was an opportunity to get his mind off the photo. He didn’t want to keep thinking about it, but it always managed to creep into his mind in the quiet moments. 

“Mamaaa…just one please. You always make them so yummy.”

“Flattery isn’t going to get you anywhere. You can have one with the rest of your classmates,” he said, kneeling down to pat her head.

“What if they eat them all,” she mumbled. 

“I’ll save you one of each,” he called back as he disappeared into the storage room. He stood in front of the shelves for a moment, finding the right size and grabbing six as Augusta’s voice floated in. 

“Papa would let me have one,” she dragged out the syllables in a sing-song voice. Mydei glanced over to the doorway where she was peeking her head in. 

A faint smile tugged at his lips. “Nice try, little one, but I’m not as weak as papa.”

Augusta let out a dramatic little sigh, finally admitting defeat. She dragged her feet a little to make a show of it, glancing at Mydei over her shoulder. When he didn’t react, she straightened up and decided skipping around the tables was more interesting. 

Mydei glanced at the overhead clock—It was almost time for them to head out. Phainon had probably gotten off work too. He’d had a busy week, so this was the first time Mydei would be seeing him since he’d left the pendant in Augusta’s room. 

His phone buzzed on one of the tables right on cue. Augusta was quick to pick it up. She gasped. “It’s papa!”

Mydei chuckled. She always got excited when he texted. “Yeah? What did he say?”

“Umm…” she looked down at the screen, thinking for a moment. “Need a…ride?”

Mydei gestured for her to pass it to him before he typed out a quick message:

Going to walk over soon.

It’s not too much, I can carry it

Phainon 

Let me pick you two up. 

No point in you carrying all those boxes while 

Augusta tries to sing to the trees

Mydei glanced over at their daughter. She was sitting on one of the chairs now, legs swinging as she hummed a little melody to herself. It sounded vaguely familiar. She paused for a second, eyebrows knitting together as she looked down at her fingers like she was trying to recount her lines.

She’d been practicing everyday in her room and hadn’t let him listen in to keep the surprise alive. She and Mydei had also picked out her outfit last week. They’d settled on a soft pink overall dress with a white blouse underneath.

He typed out a response:

She is pretty dramatic. 

Wonder where she got that from 

Phainon 

It’s genetic. Be ready in 20?

Mydei finished off with a see you then before finishing up packing the cookies. 

☼

The gymnasium was already buzzing by the time they got there. Augusta had spotted her teacher by the long table near the back, hand slipping from Phainon’s as she made a beeline for her. Mydei and Phainon weren’t far behind. 

“Miss Tribios!” She exclaimed. 

“Well hello there, Augusta. Don’t you look adorable today,” she smiled softly. “Did mama do your hair?”

Augusta flushed a little, hands twiddling behind her back. “Yes…oh! Mama brought the cookies too!”

Tribios gave him a nod as she took the boxes. “Thank you so much, Mydei. The kids are going to love these.”

“It was no trouble,” he said truthfully as she turned to face Phainon. 

“I don’t believe we’ve met,” she said, her voice kind. “I believe you’re Augusta’s papa? She talks about you all the time.”

Phainon nodded. “All good things I hope.”

Tribios gave a light laugh before she was called over by the other kindergarten class’ teacher. “Let’s let your mama and papa get settled,” she said to Augusta, taking her hand before they headed toward the stage. 

Phainon and Mydei shared a fond smile. 

There were rows of foldable chairs set out in front of the makeshift stage. The benefit of being early was that they could claim seats in the front and avoid having to knock out anyone else—Mydei knew Phainon had definitely been prepared for that. 

“Her teacher is nice,” Phainon said as he folded one leg over the other, his knee brushing against Mydei’s. 

“She likes it here,” he responded, trying not to think about the contact. 

Silence washed over them. It’d been a while since it’d been just the two of them without Augusta as a buffer. Mydei’s eyes wandered as more parents began taking their seats. Phainon cleared his throat.

“Hey, I think last week I left—” Phainon began, but the lights had started to dim and the curtains were already parting. He scrambled to pull out the digital camera he’d brought along, almost dropping it. “Oh—shit—fuck," he cursed, earning him a few glares. 

Mydei leaned over, voice low and teasing. “They’re not very keen on cursing.”

Phainon mumbled an apology, clicking the camera just as the students took their places on stage. They were dressed as sunflowers, standing in rows. Augusta was standing in the front row, a wide grin on her face as she waved to them, mouthing mama! Papa!

“She might knock someone out with that enthusiasm.”

“Wonder where she gets that from,” Mydei teased as the music began playing on the overhead speakers. 

The performance had started off pretty cohesive, but got more and more chaotic as the kids shuffled around for the choreography. Augusta had been singing the entire time, bouncing a little on her feet every time she moved.

Mydei glanced over at Phainon. He had the camera steady on her, a soft smile playing across his lips. He mouthed you’re doing great to Augusta and Mydei followed it up with a thumbs up. 

She giggled in between the lyrics, almost tripping on her feet but caught herself just in time. 

The performance ended with a round of applause. Parents began to move from their seats to congratulate their children, chat with each other, and grab some refreshments from the long table in the back. 

Phainon had his arms open for Augusta, kneeling down to catch her in his arms, but she’d ran straight past him. Phainon blinked, then looked up at Mydei with his mouth open. Both of them turned to look towards the back of the gymnasium. 

And there she was with three cookies in hand. Mydei let out a small sigh, offering Phainon a hand to get him off the floor—he was still pouting, looking like a sullen child. “Come on. Up,” Mydei said. “Before she thinks about taking another one.”

“Who cares…” he mumbled, still looking down. 

“The one who is going to have to deal with the sugar high.”

Phainon got off the floor with a groan and Mydei shook his head, tugging him toward their daughter. 

“Mama! Papa!” She exclaimed around a mouthful of crumbs, somehow still a little ball of energy as she bounced towards them. Phainon brightened up immediately, scooping her up. “Did you see? I didn’t forget anything!”

Mydei leaned in to press a kiss against her cheek. “You were amazing, babygirl.”

“Best performance I’ve ever been to,” Phainon added, tickling her stomach. Augusta giggled, offering him a bite of her chocolate chip. He leaned forward. He mumbled a thank you when she stuffed it a little too aggressively into his mouth, chewing thoughtfully. “These are incredible.”

“That’s because Mama made them,” Augusta said solemnly. “Mama’s turn!” 

She held out the cookie that Phainon had bitten, looking at him expectantly. Mydei hesitated, but he took the bite anyway, avoiding Phainon’s gaze. 

“You know what, little superstar,” Phainon began. “What do you think about dinner? You can choose the place.”

“Really?!” She lit up. 

“Well…” he dipped his voice low. “It depends on what mama says.”

She turned to Mydei, eyes shining with hope. “Mama?”

“Hmm,” Mydei hummed. It was already late and the sugar crash was definitely incoming. But, she had been so excited about tonight, and it had been a while since she got to spend time with Phainon.

“Alright, let’s go.” 

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
It was early. Way too early for Augusta’s voice to be echoing down the hallway. The sun had barely begun to rise and Mydei’s alarm hadn’t even gone off yet. 

“Mama! Mama!” her voice sounded, followed by the unmistakable patter of footsteps across the floor. 

Mydei groaned, squinting at the clock on the bedside table: 5:53 am. He buried his face further into his pillow as Augusta burst into the room.

“Wake up!” she shouted, crawling halfway on the bed and tugging at the blanket. 

“Inside voice…” Mydei muttered. 

She quickly slapped both hands over her mouth, eyes going wide before she lowered her voice. “We forgot to check the mail yesterday.”

He barely lifted his head. “Sweetheart, it’s barely six…”

“But what if it came?” she asked, tugging again. “You said it would come this week, remember?”

Mydei exhaled through his nose. He sat up with a tired grunt, running a hand through his tangled hair. “Alright,” he said, blinking sleep from his eyes. “Let’s go see.”

Augusta beamed, holding her arms up so Mydei could lift her up. He held her against his hip as they padded outside together. 

The morning air was crisp when they stepped outside. The community mailbox stood just a few feet away across the street. 

Augusta leaned forward eagerly as the mailbox door clicked open. 

He sifted through the contents, mostly bills and a few flyers until he spotted the glossy cream-coloured envelopes. Mydei handed her the one with her name written across it, watching her hug it close to her chest with glee. 

His own card was underneath it and the writing was unmistakably Castorice’s. But as he flipped through the remaining envelopes, something made his brow furrow. 

There was one more invitation. 

Phainon’s. 

Mydei stared at it for a moment, rolling his eyes. He knew exactly who did this.

“Mama?” Augusta asked, peering up at him. “Is that one for Papa?”

“Looks like it,” he said softly. He waited for a beat before turning to Augusta. “Let’s get inside. We can open them after breakfast.”

She nodded happily, letting him carry her back inside.

☼

The afternoon had gotten busy. 

It was typical for a Saturday. The weekends had always been busier after all with the pastries running low, regulars asking for refills, and students typing furiously at the tables. 

Mydei was used to it though. He moved with ease, refilling the display case and calling out polite thank yous to customers as they left, all while keeping an eye on the corner table. 

Augusta was seated there, legs swinging above the floor in a cotton dress with little flowers on it. Her hair was pulled into two buns today, a request she’d put in herself after breakfast. She had one hand cradling her chin as she stared at the door. 

The bell above the door jingled, and her body jolted upright, only to slump a second later. 

Not him. 

Mydei’s lips curved into a faint, amused smile just as Cipher strolled in. 

“Helloo~ little prince,” she greeted, leaning dramatically against the counter with an elbow. “Tell me you have cake, or I’ll have no reason to stay.”

Mydei didn’t bother answering. He slid a plate across to her. 

“Mmm,” she purred, then threw a glance over at Augusta, who was still watching the door. Cipher walked over, her boots tapping against the floor, and gently patted the little girl’s head. “What are you up to, little one?”

“Waiting for papa,” Augusta replied, her voice soft as she tilted her face up. “We’re going to the library.”

“Oh?” Cipher’s brows rose, and she pulled up a chair to sit beside her. “How domestic,” she murmured, glancing pointedly at Mydei.

He didn’t look up as he passed a customer a box of scones. “Do you wanna tell me why I got Phainon’s invitation?”

Cipher gasped, her hand flying to her chest. “Don’t look at me. It wasn’t my idea.”

“Mmhmm,” Mydei arched an eyebrow. 

“Okay fiiiine, you caught me,” she sighed, poking her fork into the slice. “But in my defence, I thought you two would be—” she made a suggestive gesture with her fingers “—by now.”

“You’re something else.”

She grinned. “Well, you did let him knock you up.”

Mydei’s face didn’t change, but Augusta’s did. She frowned, eyes narrowing. “What does ‘knock up’ mean?”

Cipher didn’t even blink. “It’s when—”

“Cipher,” Mydei cut in, shooting her a glare.

“Relaaxxx~” she said with a groan, dragging out the word like she was the one being wronged. “I wasn’t even going to say anything bad.”

Before he could respond, the bell above the door chimed again. 

This time, Augusta launched to her feet, chair scraping across the floor as she dashed over to the door. 

“Papa! Papa!”

Phainon had barely stepped inside when she collided into his legs. He caught her mid-jump, scooping her up into his arms. 

“Hey—careful there,” he chuckled. 

“Look! Look! I got my invitation!” she beamed, holding up the envelope. 

Phainon took it, inspecting it. “Ah, fancy,” he murmured, lifting his gaze toward Cipher. “Although I didn’t get mine yet…”

Cipher pointed both hands at the counter. “Talk to your co-parent.”

Mydei reached under the register and pulled out the third envelope, handing it over. 

“There was a… mix-up in delivery,” he said. 

Phainon accepted it without hesitation, their fingers brushing. “Oh well, no matter,” he said lightly, slipping it into his coat pocket. 

For a moment, the silence between them lingered. It wasn’t heavy anymore like it had once been. Phainon’s gaze met his, those stupid blue eyes impossible to ignore. Mydei was the first to glance away. 

“I’ll have her back in a couple hours,” Phainon said, adjusting Augusta in his arms. 

“Don’t let her charm her way into ice cream.”

“Mamaaa!” Augusta whined. 

“No promises,” Phainon murmured as he pressed a kiss to her cheek. “What Mama doesn’t know won’t hurt him.”

Cipher let out a low whistle under her breath once Phainon and Augusta had left. “I didn’t know it was that bad.”

“What are you talking about?” Mydei asked. 

She grinned, taking another bite of cake. “Nothing,” she said, far too pleased with herself. 

☼

The knock came just as Mydei stepped out of the bathroom, still toweling off his hair in front of the mirror in nothing but worn sweatpants that clung low on his hips. Steam curled into the hallway behind him as he padded toward the door. 

“Coming,” he called out before grabbing the nearest clean T-shirt. He tugged it on quickly and cracked the door open. 

Augusta was bouncing on her heels in the hallway, her cheeks flushed and a bright smile on her face as she clutched a plush orange cat. 

“Mama!” she wrapped her arms around his leg. “Look! Papa won this for me! He said it reminds him of you and his name is Fig Stew!”

Phainon, who stood behind her with his hands tucked into his pocket, cleared his throat.

Augusta froze, her eyes going wide as she realized what she’d blurted out. “Oh…I wasn’t supposed to say that…” she said shyly, peering back at Phainon over her shoulder with a guilty look. 

Mydei raised an eyebrow, the corner of his mouth twitching. “Oh? And here I thought you two were at the library.”

“We were,” Phainon said. “We just… took a little detour on the way back.”

“And we definitely didn’t have ice cream,” Augusta said solemnly as if she hadn't just told on herself. 

Mydei narrowed his eyes playfully, but he didn’t press. Instead, he nudged her gently toward the hallway. “Alright, go wash up. Dinner’s just about ready.”

Phainon’s gaze followed her as she scampered off, her giggles fading down the hall.

“She’s very persuasive,” he mumbled when she was out of earshot. 

“Hmm.” Mydei hummed just slightly, tossing him a look over his shoulder. “Or you’re just weak.” 

Phainon gave a quiet laugh, and Mydei hesitated for only a beat before speaking again. 

“Do you…want to stay for dinner?”

Phainon blinked as if he were caught off guard. “Are you sure?”

“I wouldn’t have asked if I wasn’t,” Mydei replied, already walking toward the kitchen. 

Augusta rounded the corner, water dripping from her fingertips. She stopped just short of the table when she saw Phainon still standing there. “Papa! You’re staying?!”

Phainon glanced at Mydei and gave her a soft smile. “Yeah. I’m staying.”

Augusta clapped her hands together, clearly delighted by the fact, and darted to the table to set it the same way she’d seen Mydei do. 

Mydei busied himself in the kitchen, pulling out the stew, that had been warming from, the oven. “Go ahead and sit,” he told Phainon. “I’ll bring everything over.”

Phainon shrugged off his coat and slung it over the back of a chair. He took the seat across from Augusta, who was practically buzzing from excitement. 

Dinner was nice. Phainon listened to Augusta’s stories, teased her a little, and even complimented Mydei’s cooking. And for a moment, it felt seamless. Normal even. Like whatever this was could’ve been routine.

But eventually, time made itself known.

Phainon glanced at the clock and stood. “Ah…I should probably get going. It’s getting late.”

“No!” Augusta said immediately, her eyes wide. 

Phainon hesitated. “Hey, we’ll see each other soon, alright?”

But her bottom lip was trembling now. She pushed off her chair. “No!” she said louder this time, walking over quickly and grabbing onto his sleeve. “Don’t leave, papa. Please stay.”

“Sweetheart,” Mydei began gently, kneeling down in front of her. “Papa’s just going home to sleep. You got to spend the day together. You’ll see him again another day.”

“No!” Augusta’s voice broke into a sob as she shook her head. “I don’t want him to leave, why does he have to leave?!”

She was crying now, her hands trying to pull Phainon back by the sleeve. “Please stay! Please! Please!”

“Hey, hey,” Phainon knelt down, pulling her into his arms. “I promise I’m not going far. I’ll see you tomorrow, babygirl.”

“Everyone else’s mamas and papas stay!” she choked out, pushing her face into his shoulder. 

The weight of that landed harder than either of them expected. 

“Augusta,” Mydei swallowed the lump in his throat before speaking softly, “You know it’s different for us.”

“But why…” she whimpered. “Why can’t papa just stay?”

Phainon closed his eyes, guilt flickering across his face as he held her closer. Mydei sighed, but when their eyes met, there was a moment of stillness. 

He gave the faintest nod.

It took a few more minutes and a lot of gentle coaxing before she calmed down. Her cheeks were flushed and damp with tears as she rubbed her eyes with her sleeves.

Mydei stroked her hair back, voice soft. “Go brush your teeth, okay? Papa will tuck you in tonight.”

“Promise?”

“I promise,” Phainon placed a hand over his chest. “I’ll stay.”

Augusta hesitated for a moment before she padded over to the bathroom, throwing a glance over her shoulder like she was making sure Phainon wasn’t leaving. 

When she finally disappeared into the bathroom, Phainon stood a little awkwardly. 

“Sorry…” he trailed off, rubbing the back of his neck. “I’ll leave after she falls asleep.”

Mydei shook his head. “She’ll be upset in the morning. Just…stay,” he’d said the last part a little softer than he’d meant to. 

☼

It was sometime past midnight when Mydei stirred awake. Augusta had gone down without a fight knowing that Phainon was going to stay with her, but it still didn’t stop the guilt from eating away at him. 

She’d been so happy lately, and Mydei had almost forgotten that Phainon’s return was as much a shift in her world as it was in his. Even with all her excitement, it had to be confusing. This version of a family that didn’t quite fit into the boxes that her friends had. 

He let out a soft sigh as he swung his legs over the side of the bed and pushed himself up. He didn’t bother pulling on a shirt as he padded into the kitchen. 

Phainon stood there in the dark, the fridge’s glow highlighting the sharp angles of his face. His hair was a little messy, and he looked like he hadn’t expected anyone to catch him mid-search. 

“I didn’t mean to wake you,” he said in a hushed tone, his hand pausing mid-reach by the cupboard. 

“You didn’t,” Mydei murmured, stepping into the kitchen and becoming hyperaware of the fact that he was, in fact, half naked in front of Phainon. Not that it was anything Phainon hadn’t seen before, but it was different now. “Thirsty?”

“What?” Phainon snapped a little too quickly, flushing immediately as if he’d been caught thinking about something else entirely. “Oh. Yeah. Water.”

Mydei tilted his head, an amused smirk playing at his lips. “You looking for a glass?”

Phainon gave a sheepish nod. 

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes and reached past him, not quite brushing against him but it was close enough. He grabbed a glass from the shelf, filling it up with cold water and handed it over. Their fingers brushed, a brief touch, but enough to make the moment feel just a little too intimate. 

"Thanks,” Phainon said, voice a little rough. 

Mydei leaned back against the counter, folding his arms over his chest. “Couldn’t sleep?”

Phainon took a sip. “Turns out beds made for four year olds aren’t great for grown men.”

Mydei chuckled faintly, but then his gaze dropped, lingering on Phainon’s chest for a moment. 

Phainon noticed the shift. “Hey… I meant to ask you earlier—I think I left a pendant here the other week.” 

Mydei pushed off the counter and walked toward the drawer by the TV. “I found it in Augusta’s room.”

Phainon followed behind as Mydei rummaged through the drawer until he found the chain, handing it over to Phainon. 

Phainon smiled softly at the sight of it, letting out a sigh of relief. “Thanks…I thought I’d lost it for good.” He paused for a moment. “Do you think you could…?”

Mydei blinked, a little caught off guard, but he nodded. He stepped behind Phainon. The clasp was finicky, and the chain caught once, but he managed. His fingers brushed against Phainon’s skin. He still had that sun tattoo on the side of his neck. 

Phainon adjusted the pendant once it was secure, holding the locket gently against his chest before tucking it beneath his shirt.

“You wear it all the time?” Mydei asked. 

“...Yeah.”

Mydei let out a quiet breath. “Why—” his voice caught. “Why do you keep that photo inside?”

Phainon’s gaze dropped. “Wanted to have something to remember you by.” he said softly. 

Mydei didn’t answer at first. His eyes were fixed on the floor, but when Phainon took a small step forward, he looked up.

“I remember when I took it,” Phainon said, his voice fond. 

“So do I.”

Their voices barely broke the silence. Phainon stepped closer again, the distance between them closing, but this time Mydei didn’t look away. 

He felt Phainon’s fingers barely graze his wrist. Their faces were close enough that Mydei could see every shift in his expression, every shallow breath. He didn’t mean to tilt his head but he did. And Phainon didn’t move away. 

Their lips hovered just apart, eyes fluttering shut. It was like the world had narrowed to just the two of them and Mydei’s chest ached with longing. It had been so long. He hadn’t been with anyone since—not seriously at least. 

And It was finally happening. 

And then—

Honk!

A sharp car horn outside shattered the quiet. Both of them jolted slightly, blinking out of the moment and suddenly realizing what was happening.

Phainon let out a breathy laugh, stepping back just an inch. 

Mydei rubbed the back of his neck, a faint flush creeping up his throat. 

“I should probably head back before she notices I’m gone.”

“Right,” Mydei said, averting his gaze in an attempt to try and hide the flush in his cheeks. “Goodnight.”

“...Goodnight, Mydei.”

But neither of them wanted to be the first to go. 

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.html:
Mydei was going through inventory in the afternoon. The bakery was closed for the day, so it was the perfect opportunity. He stood behind the counter with his sleeves rolled up and a pen tucked behind his ear as he sorted through some papers on his clipboard. 

He muttered under his breath as he cross-referenced the week’s numbers while the floorboards creaked upstairs—two thumps followed by the sound of muffled laughter. He couldn’t help but smile.

Phainon hadn’t left in the morning. He was still upstairs, keeping Augusta entertained. Mydei had told himself it was fine even if breakfast was awkward. They hadn’t said much to each other after last night, but Augusta deserved more time with him. Still, it didn’t stop the thoughts from creeping in. 

Every time he paused, he thought about the night before. The quiet of the house, how soft Phainon’s eyes had seemed, how that gentleness had been reserved for him. How their fingers had brushed and how close they had been. Mydei could still feel the ghost of Phainon’s touch, the warmth of his skin, and how he could feel his own heartbeat in his throat. 

He tried not to think about what would’ve happened if that car horn hadn’t interrupted them.

He was pulled out of his thoughts when the door swung open

“Your favourite brides are here~” Cipher said, breezing in with her hand in Castorice’s.

Castorice gave a small wave. “Good morning, Mydei.”

“Morning,” he muttered, still looking down at the papers, brows furrowed in concentration until two fingers flicked sharply against his forehead.

“Ow—what was that for?”

“We’re gracing you with our presence and you’re not even looking up,” Cipher said, arms crossed. 

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes, lifting his gaze to meet her. “Forgive me for not having the red carpet ready.”

Before either of them could say anything, the sound of footsteps on the stairs sounded—heavier ones followed by little ones. 

“I’m way too young to be a grandfather,” Phainon’s playful voice filtered downstairs. 

“But look! She’s so cute,” Augusta insisted. 

Moments later, the two of them appeared. Phainon was holding one of Augusta’s plushies like it were a baby, and Augusta trailed behind him with a little skip in her step. 

“Well, well, well, what do we have here?” Cipher raised a brow. 

Phainon stopped mid-step, clearly not expecting company. “Oh—uh, hi.”

“Oh uh hi, he says,” Cipher mocked. 

“Papa slept over!” Augusta announced brightly, bouncing on her feet. 

Castorice flushed as she looked between the two men, and Cipher narrowed her eyes. She crouched down in front of Augusta, patting her head. 

“Hey little one,” she began. “Where did papa sleep?”

“With me!” Augusta chirped proudly. 

“Oh boo~ that’s not fun,” she frowned. 

“Why not?” Augusta titled her head curiously. 

Before Cipher could say something that would earn her a scolding, Castorice cut in smoothly, kneeling beside her. “Auntie Cipher is just being silly. Did you like having papa sleeping over?”

“Mhm!” Augusta nodded, but then she tapped her chin. She glanced over at Phainon, then at Mydei, who tried very hard not to interrupt whatever this interrogation was. Finally, she spoke again. “But papa snores,” she added. “And he squished me!”

“I don’t snore,” Phainon defended, placing the plushie on the counter beside him. 

“Debatable,” Mydei muttered under his breath, a smile tugging at the corners of his mouth as he tucked the papers and clipboard away. 

Phainon leaned over the counter, propping himself on his elbows. His hands moved slowly as he reached toward Mydei’s face, fingertips brushing his cheek in a moment so brief and gentle that it had Mydei’s heart skipping a beat. 

“Pen,” Phainon said simply, plucking it from behind his ear and holding up to him. 

Cipher gasped and covered Augusta’s eyes with both eyes. “Please. Not in front of the child. She shouldn’t have to see this. It’s too much.”

Augusta just giggled, oblivious to what Cipher meant. 

“You’re insufferable,” Mydei muttered as he took the pen back. 

Castorice stifled a laugh, scooping up Augusta in her arms and gave her a little spin while Cipher leaned in close to Phainon, whispering something that made his ears go pink. 

Mydei didn’t bother asking what it was. 

☼ 

The boutique was quiet save for the rustle of fabric and the occasional chatter from the attendants. Mydei stood just to the side of the pedestal, arms crossed as Castorice examined herself in the mirror. 

The dress she wore was simple and elegant with a light shimmer when it caught the sunlight. It flowed around her with cascading layers of silk. 

Augusta twirled in circles nearby, her arms stretched out like a little dancer. “It’s so pretty!” she exclaimed for the third time, nearly tripping over the edge of the fitting platform. “You look like a princess, Auntie Cas!”

Castorice blushed faintly, smoothing a hand over the fabric. “Thank you, sunshine.”

“You’re going to be the prettiest one there,” Augusta said, skipping over to Mydei and grabbing onto his hand. “Right, mama?”

Mydei chuckled and bent down to kiss the top of her head. “Absolutely.”

“You should keep it forever and wear it all the time,” Augusta sighed wistfully. 

“That’s the plan,” Castorice smiled. 

“Even in the bath?”

“Well, maybe not there,” she said, exhaling a little, her fingers brushing the fabric again like she couldn’t believe it was real. 

One of the boutique attendants stepped forward with pins and tape measure. As they worked, Mydei stepped back slightly as Augusta plopped down on one of the stools. She gestured for Mydei to come closer. 

“Mama,” she whispered and Mydei crouched down to lean into her. “When are you getting married?”

Mydei chuckled a little. “Not anytime soon.”

“Oh…” she trailed off, looking a little disappointed. 

He leaned in to kiss her cheek, tucking a strand of her hair behind her ear. “I already have you and you, little miss, are a handful,” he teased, tickling her stomach.

☼

“Mama! I like this one,” Augusta declared, twirling in front of the mirror. Her dress fluttered as she spun. It was a pale lilac one with tiny embroidered flowers on the skirt. Mydei watched her with soft eyes. 

“Well, it’s about time,” Phainon said and Mydei lightly kicked his shin. 

“It’s perfect, sweetheart.”

Since the wedding was coming up, Mydei had decided it was time to take Augusta dress shopping. He’d texted Phainon to see if he wanted to tag along—mainly because he knew it’d make Augusta happy. 

Augusta turned around, smoothing down the skirt. “Do I have to take it off?”

“Yes,” Mydei said, nudging her back toward the changing room. “We can’t have you attending the wedding with a stained dress,” 

Augusta frowned, turning to look at Phainon instead. “Papa?” she asked sweetly, looking up at him with big eyes. 

Phainon looked away and Mydei playfully rolled his eyes knowing that Phainon was still weak to those eyes. “What Mama said,” he said, but it lacked conviction. 

Augusta knit her brows together, but slipped into the changing room anyways. 

There was a beat of silence between him and Phainon. It had been like this lately whenever their daughter wasn’t there as a buffer. Mydei knew they needed to talk. Not just about her , but about them.  

“Mamaaa!” Augusta’s shriek cut through the silence. “I’m stuck!”

Mydei shook his head fondly, going into the changing room to see the dress stuck over Augusta’s head. He clicked his tongue gently before he pried her out of it, watching as she sighed a breath of relief as if she’d thought it’d never come off. 

He helped her into the clothes she’d come in with before they headed to the register. 

He was about to pull out his wallet, but Phainon had already beaten him to it with a soft: “Let me. It’s for her.”

Mydei didn’t protest. 

They were walking towards the exit, shopping bag in hand, and Augusta skipping just ahead of them when she stopped. 

“Can we take pictures?” she asked. 

Mydei followed her gaze to the corner, where a small photobooth stood. It looked like it hadn’t been used for a while, but the screen was on and Augusta was already making a beeline toward it.

She poked her head out from behind the curtain. “Come on!” 

Mydei and Phainon waited a beat before following her inside. 

The booth was cramped to say the least. Augusta sat between them on the narrow bench, buzzing with excitement. 

The countdown for the first shot began; Augusta and Phainon grinned while Mydei just gave a soft smile. In the second photo, both Augusta and Phainon stuck their tongues out and Mydei gave a soft sigh at how in-sync they were. 

“Kiss!” Augusta said right before the third photo, pointing to her own cheeks. Mydei kissed one side of her cheek while Phainon leaned in to kiss the other. The flash went off just before Augusta’s smile turned into giggles. 

The final photo caught the two of them looking at each other with soft eyes while Augusta just smiled into the camera with a happy grin. 

Augusta hit the print button, the machine whirring lightly when she darted out from behind the curtain, her shoes skidding against the tile floor as she beelined for the photo tray.

“I’m gonna watch them print!” she called out. 

Mydei shifted slightly, trying to step out of the booth himself, but Phainon had moved at the same time. Their hips bumped. 

Then their shoulders. 

Then somehow Mydei stepped on Phainon’s boot and Phainon backed up too quickly and lost his balance. 

Mydei reached to steady him but ended up toppling backward into the bench with a quiet grunt, the cushion doing nothing to break the fall. Phainon caught himself just in time to keep him from crushing him completely, hands braced on either side of Mydei’s head. 

“...You okay?” Phainon asked. 

Still pinned by proximity, Mydei stared up at him. He could feel the heat from Phainon’s body and his own heartbeat slamming against his chest. 

But Phainon didn’t move.

Neither did he. 

And then Phainon leaned in just slightly, and Mydei didn’t stop him. He couldn’t. Not when they were this close. Not when Phainon’s gaze dropped to his lips like that. Mydei’s breath caught just as their noses brushed. 

Click. 

Click. 

Mydei blinked and Phainon paused. 

The sound of the camera shutter firing again echoed through the booth and they both turned to look at the flashing countdown on the screen. 

3…2…1

The curtain was yanked open by Augusta, holding up the strip of photos of the three of them, but her mouth shaped into a little ‘o’ when she saw them. 

She stared at the screen and then at the two of them again: Phainon still hovering over Mydei with one knee on the bench, Mydei’s hands bunched in Phainon’s shirt. 

“Mama! Papa! How could you take pictures without me!”

“We weren’t,” Mydei said quickly, sitting up. 

Phainon coughed and scooted back, smoothing down his shirt. “We were just—uh—” he turned to Mydei for help, clearly unsure of how to explain. 

Augusta squinted at them suspiciously. Then, she walked over to the screen hit print before either of them could protest. Mydei pinched the bridge of his nose as Phainon followed their daughter out. 

Mydei waited a moment before going after them. 

The strip of photos slid out of the machine and Augusta picked up. 

She gasped. “This one’s so funny… Papa, you look like a tomato!”

Phainon reached out and took it from her fingers before she could inspect the photos any further. “Not for little eyes,” he muttered.

 “Let’s… not put this one on the fridge, okay?” Mydei added. 

Augusta looked a little confused but nodded anyway. 

☼ 

Augusta had fallen asleep on the way home and Mydei had tucked her in with a kiss. He flicked off the overhead light, leaving only her nightlight on. He stood in the doorway for a couple of minutes to make sure she’d actually gone to sleep before he made his way into the living room. 

Phainon was sitting on the couch, scrolling through his phone. He glanced up at the sound of Mydei’s footsteps, tucking it away. He had asked Phainon to stay. 

Not for Augusta this time—but for himself.

They needed to talk.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
They both opened their mouths at the same time. 

“Why did you—” Phainon started, just as—

“We need to—” Mydei began. 

Both of their words faltered. Mydei wasn’t even sure where to begin. He had a feeling this conversation wasn’t going to be pleasant. The air had shifted between them after he’d put Augusta to bed, the silence stretching a lot heavier than before. Still, Phainon nodded for him to continue.

Mydei exhaled slowly and leaned forward, bracing his elbows on his knees. 

“I don’t know what we’re doing,” he admitted quietly. “I know it isn’t supposed to be easy. I know we’re both…trying. But I just want to do right by our daughter. It’s all I’ve ever wanted. And I don’t think…” He gestured vaguely between them, unable to meet Phainon’s eyes. “Whatever this is between us is right for her.”

Phainon’s brows drew together, face unreadable beneath the dim lights. “What are you trying to say?”

“I think we need…boundaries,” Mydei said, more firmly now, though his voice still trembled. He didn’t want to be the one to have to say this. He didn’t want to let go. “Like a schedule. Days when you can see her, weekends she stays with you. We can give her a…routine.”

Phainon’s mouth pulled into a frown. He didn’t argue or protest right away. Instead, he looked at Mydei like he was searching for something. Some crack in his resolve or maybe some hint that he didn’t mean what he was saying. 

“Mydei…” he said softly, reaching up. His fingertips brushed the side of Mydei’s face gently. “Is that what you really want?”

Mydei startled slightly at the touch, flinching. He reached up, hand brushing Phainon’s away. It wasn’t harsh, but it was enough to put some space between them. 

“When you found out about her,” he said slowly, “you told me you hadn’t forgiven me. And I understood that. But now… can you honestly say that’s changed?”

Phainon opened his mouth then closed it again. He didn’t speak. 

Mydei let out a shaky breath, eyes closing for a moment. 

“Because if you haven’t,” his voice caught in his throat, “then…a part of you is always going to resent me. Even if you don’t say it, even if you think you can chew it up and swallow it down. I don’t want it to be held over my head for the rest of our lives.”

“I wouldn’t do that,” Phainon said quickly. 

“Then have you forgiven me?”

Another pause. 

It was longer this time. 

And heavier. 

Phainon looked down at his hands, but he didn’t respond. 

And that was all the answer Mydei needed. 

He nodded, more to himself than to Phainon, feeling the tightness in his chest. He’d let his wishful thinking get the best of him. How foolish. 

“Then I suppose we have our answer.”

It hurt more than he thought it would—saying it and letting it settle between them. But maybe it was a good thing. Maybe this was how he could finally let go. 

☼

The afternoon was slower than usual, so Mydei had run out of excuses when Augusta had insisted on helping. 

She hadn’t been back from school for long, still in the same clothes with her sleeves slightly rolled up to match the way he did his as she stood on a stool behind the counter. She flashed a bright smile at every customer that walked in, hands folded neatly in front of her

Mydei stood just behind her with a fond smile tugging at his lips as he tapped in each other she announced. Most of the regulars knew her by now, offering a wave or asking about what she’d been up to lately. 

Still, there were still the odd newcomers who came in surprised with comments like ‘oh my is she yours?’ or ‘she looks just like you’.

The bell above the door jingled again, and Augusta’s eyes went wide. 

“Miss Tribios! What are you doing here?!”

She laughed as she stepped inside. “Hello Augusta—Mydei,” she added with a knowing smile toward him. “I thought I’d stop by before heading home.”

“So you’re going back to school?” Augusta asked, almost in awe. 

Tribios shook her head. “I don’t live at school, sweetheart. I’m going back to my home, just like you do after class.”

“Oh.” Augusta said thoughtfully, still looking troubled by the revelation. 

“How about you take Miss Tribios’ order, hm?” Mydei offered gently. 

“Of course!” Augusta snapped back into her usual chipper self, lacing her fingers together. “What would you like today, Miss Tribios?”

“Well… what do you recommend?”

“An expresso and a carrot cake muffin.”

Tribios let out a warm laugh. “You’re training her young, aren’t you?”

“She’s a natural,” Mydei said fondly as he began to pack the grounds, watching as Augusta passed over a packaged muffin. 

Just as Tribios took the muffin, the door opened again. This time, Phainon stepped inside wearing dark sunglasses and a navy coat. Mydei always liked the way that colour looked on him. 

It had been a while since they had actually spent time together especially after they’d talked that night. Mydei couldn’t believe it’d almost been a month since then. 

As always, Augusta lit up as soon as she saw him.

“Papa!”

Before Mydei could stop her, she was half-leaning over the counter like she was ready to leap over it. Phainon crossed the floor quickly and caught her easily, hoisting her up into his arms. 

“Helping mama, huh?” he asked, tapping her nose. 

“Yes! I even took real orders.”

Phainon chuckled, brushing some of her out of her face. “Then I think it’s time for my little barista to clock out.” 

She giggled, looping her arms around his neck. He looked over at Mydei, raising an eyebrow. “What do you say, boss?”

“Mhm,” Mydei nodded. “Just don’t let her get grass stains on her pants this time,” he added with a pointed look and both of them nodded. 

Mydei caught Phainon’s eyes just before they headed out. He gave him a lingering look before they were gone. 

Mydei busied himself wiping down the counter. 

He glanced up just as Tribios was about to head out. She was gathering her things from a nearby table when he spoke. “May I ask you something?”

She nodded. 

“Does Augusta…” he hesitated. “Is she doing alright at school?”

There was a beat of silence, and Tribios’ expression shifted into something more thoughtful. “You’re worried about how she’s adjusting.”

He nodded. 

“She seems happy,” she said carefully. “She’s bright and she has no trouble communicating her thoughts. That doesn’t mean she doesn’t have questions though, but… as far as split households go, you’re doing a better job than most.”

Mydei sighed, leaning against the counter now. “I just—I worry about her getting confused. About Phainon and I.”

Tribios tilted her head. “She’s a perceptive young girl. Children usually are. Sometimes we underestimate how much they can understand, especially when we avoid saying everything out loud.”

Mydei nodded thoughtfully. “We’ve been trying to give her some structure. But sometimes, it feels like she’s confused. 

She looked at him for a long moment, then offered him a soft smile. 

“Well,” she said, lifting her drink. “If I hadn’t known better, I would’ve thought you and Phainon were together.”

Mydei blinked. “We’re not.”

She shrugged with a twinkle in her eyes. “Could’ve fooled me with the way he looks at you.”

And with that, she headed for the door, leaving Mydei standing alone, unsure of what to think. 

☼

Mydei was folding one of Augusta’s soft cotton t-shirts when he glanced over at the small pile of clothes already sitting neatly in her overnight bag. He tucked it in alongside her pajamas, a sweater and a few pairs of socks. 

Across the bed, Augusta was swinging her legs while humming to herself. She had already taken it upon herself to what she had deemed essential—Fig Stew, her compact mirror shaped like a strawberry, and a handful of markers.

She wouldn’t be leaving until tomorrow evening, but Mydei didn’t want to be scrambling last and have her forget anything. He knew how important this was to Phainon, especially since it would be his first time having her overnight. 

“Mama?” Augusta asked suddenly. 

Mydei glanced up at her. “Mhm?”

“Are you going to come with me?”

He paused for a beat before shaking his head gently. “This weekend is just you and papa,” he reminded her. “Remember what we talked about? How sometimes you’ll be staying with him? 

Augusta frowned in thought. “But…why can’t papa stay here instead?” she asked. “He could sleep in my room like last time. Or in your bed—it’s bigger!”

Mydei hoisted himself up onto the bed to sit down beside her, resting a gentle hand on her back. “Papa and I aren’t together, sweetheart,” he explained. “Not like grandma and grandpa or like auntie Cas and Cipher.”

Augusta tilted her head. “Why not?”

He hesitated. “Because… sometimes grown-ups care about each other, but things don’t always work out the way they hoped.” he tried in a way she’d be able to understand. 

“But you always smile when papa’s here,” she said, voice quieter, playing with her fingers. 

Mydei gave her a soft smile, leaning in to kiss her cheek and pulling her into his side. “That’s because papa makes you happy,” he settled on saying even if it wasn’t entirely the truth. She looked a little disappointed at that response. 

Mydei tilted her chin upwards. “Hey… that doesn’t mean that we don’t love you. That’s never going to change, sweetheart.”

Augusta was silent for a moment, seeming like she was taking it all in. “Did you and papa have a fight?” she asked. “Miss Tribios always says when you fight, you should say sorry.”

Mydei reached out to pull her into his lap this time. “That’s very good advice, but papa and I aren’t fighting. We’re just…” Mydei trailed off. “Trying to do our best.” 

“But we used to do things together,” she murmured. 

“I know,” Mydei nodded. “And we still might do things together, but it’ll be different.”

Augusta was quiet again. “Then did I do something wrong? I’ll say sorry to papa and then he can come here again!” she added quickly. 

Mydei’s heart dropped. 

“No,” he replied, wrapping his arms around her. “No, babygirl. This isn’t because of you. You didn’t do anything wrong. Grown-ups… we make mistakes. And sometimes it takes us a while to figure out what’s best. But you’re the best thing that ever happened to me and I don’t ever want you thinking it’s your fault.”

She leaned against his chest with a small nod, her fingers curled into his shirt. 

Mydei held her close for a few more moments before kissing the top of her head. “And besides, you’re going to have a lot of fun this weekend and you’ll see your room.”

“Really?” she asked, eyes shining again. 

“Mhm,” Mydei nodded. “Papa has it all set up. He’s been working on it for a while.”

That finally made her smile.

☼

Mydei had been in the kitchen since early morning even though it was his day off, but with the wedding approaching, he’d needed to plan out the details of the cake properly.

It wasn’t the one he’d be making for them just yet, but he thought he’d make one as a test on a smaller scale. He stood at the counter with a piping bag in one hand, a sample tier turning slowly on the lazy susan. He hadn’t decided whether to transport the finished cake or to just take the tiers and finish up at the venue yet.

Augusta had her own job too. She was sitting on the counter, holding a small spoon, eyes wide every time Mydei gave her a new filling or piece of cake to sample. There were a few smudges of icing on her cheeks—Mydei had just clicked his tongue and wiped her face as she giggled. 

“This one is the pistachio one,” Mydei said, offering her a little bite, but she made a face. 

“I liked the chocolate one better,” she said. 

Mydei huffed a laugh, shaking his head. “Of course you do,” he said just as the door opened, followed by the sound of familiar footsteps. 

Phainon stepped into the bakery, hair a little wind-swepted. “Smells good in here,” he said, raising an eyebrow. 

“Papa! Mama’s testing for the wedding cake!” Augusta chirped. “You have to try the chocolate one.”

Phainon chuckled, making his way over. “Well, if you insist…”

Mydei rolled his eyes playfully but reached for a fork anyways. He sliced off a small piece, holding it out between them. “Here.”

He expected Phainon to take the fork from him, maybe mumble a ‘thanks’. But instead, Phainon leaned forward without hesitation and took the bite. 

Mydei froze, a little stunned, still holding the utensil between them. 

Phainon didn’t seem to care much though. “Holy shit,” he muttered. 

Augusta gasped, jumping off the counter and pointing an accusatory finger at him. “Papa! You said a bad word! That’s a timeout word!”

Phainon flinched, throwing Mydei a guilty glance. 

Mydei crossed his arms. 

“Okay, okay, I know, my bad. Can I get a pass this time?” he asked, crouching down to their daughter’s level.

Augusta pursed her lips for a moment before nodded, and Phainon pulled her in for a hug while mouthing ‘sorry’ to Mydei. 

“Alright, come on, sunshine,” Phainon began, pulling away to look at Augusta. “Let's get going before mama gets really mad at me.”

She giggled, skipping over to grab her overnight bag. Mydei crouched down to give her a hug and kiss. 

“Be good, okay? And don’t try to bribe papa. You know he’s weak.”

Phainon pouted. “I am not.”

“You are,” Mydei said flatly. 

“Okay…maybe, but just look at her.”

Augusta nodded proudly, holding onto Phainon’s hand as they headed toward the door. But then, she paused to look back at Mydei and darted back. “One more hug!”

Mydei caught her with ease, wrapping his arms around her and pressing another soft kiss to her cheek. “Have fun, sweetheart. Call me if you need anything.”

She nodded into his shoulder before stepping back and grabbing Phainon’s hand again. 

The two of them left soon after that, chatting away. Still, Phainon glanced back long enough for Mydei to meet his eyes. 

☼

The rain had started somewhere between midnight and one, starting off soft, then heavier against the windows. Mydei stirred once, vaguely registering it in his sleep, but didn’t fully wake until the sharp knock sounded at the door. 

He was still in his sweatpants and black tank top when he padded across the floor, cracking the door open slightly at first. 

Phainon stood there with Augusta in his arms. She was half asleep but tears streaked her cheeks and clinging tightly to him. 

“I’m sorry,” Phainon said quietly. “She wouldn’t sleep. She kept saying she missed you.”

Mydei outstretched his arms for her. Augusta curled into him immediately, rubbing soothing circles against her back to calm her down. 

“Hey, sweetheart,” Mydei murmured. “You okay?”

“I just…” sniffled. “I missed you, mama.”

His chest ached, but he smiled and kissed her temple. “I know, it’s okay.” He knelt to set her down on her feet gently. “Why don’t you go lie down in bed? It’s been a long night.”

She nodded, rubbing one eye with her fist and made her to her bedroom. 

Mydei turned back to Phainon. “You didn’t have to bring her back.”

“I didn’t want to push her,” he admitted. “She was getting really upset. I thought she’d calm down, but it just got worse.”

Mydei softened. “It’s not your fault. She’s never been away from me before. She’ll get used to it… it might take some time though.”

Phainon nodded, eyes tired. He lingered in the doorway. “I should get going, let you two sleep.”

Mydei nodded. He closed the door, a little hesitant. 

He glanced over at the window. The rain was really coming down and it was already late. Before he could think about it any further, he was already slipping his shoes on. 

Mydei hadn’t realized how fast he was moving until he was outside. He caught Phainon by the arm just by the doorway.

Phainon turned, startled. His hair was damp from the rain and his shirt had already been soaked, clinging to his skin. 

“Stay,” Mydei said, his voice low.

“Mydei—”

“Don’t be stupid,” he cut in. “You shouldn’t be driving like this.”

For a beat, Phainon hesitated. But then he gave a breathless nod and followed Mydei back inside without another word, arms wrapped loosely around himself to keep him from the cold. 

Upstairs, Mydei moved quickly, tossing him a towel and heading to grab dry clothes from his room. He didn’t expect Phainon to follow, but he did quietly. 

Phainon caught the towel when Mydei tossed it over and began rubbing his hair. “Thanks,” he muttered. 

Mydei glanced back just as Phainon peeled off his wet shirt, water trailing down the clean lines of his chest and abdomen. Mydei blinked and turned back to the drawer, grabbing a plain shirt while trying not to think about the rising heat in his cheeks. 

He turned with it in hand, ready to pass it over, but Phainon reached out and caught his wrist instead. 

“I do,” Phainon said, voice a little unsteady as he tugged Mydei closer. “I do forgive you, Mydei.” His name came out like a whisper. 

“Phai—” he started, but Phainon was already shaking his head. 

“I’ve tried,” he continued. “I’ve really tried to do this whole co-parenting thing. To tell myself that we’re just doing this for Augusta, but every time I see you…” he trailed off, eyes searching Mydei’s. “I think about what I should’ve told you more than five years ago. Maybe then, things would have turned out differently, maybe then you wouldn’t have thought twice about telling me.”

Mydei stood there, stunned. The shirt slipped from his fingers. His lips parted, but he couldn’t find the words. 

Phainon stepped in close. Close enough that Mydei could feel the heat from his bare skin. He brought a hand up to Mydei’s jaw, the other settling lightly on his waist, like he was giving him the chance to pull away. 

Mydei didn’t. 

Then Phainon leaned in. “I would never hold it over your head,” he whispered, barely a breath before his lips met Mydei’s.

The kiss started tentative—soft. Phainon’s lips brushed against his like a question. But the moment Mydei titled his head and leaned into it, it deepened. The world slowed to that moment, the sound of the rain drowning out as warmth pooled in the pit of Mydei’s stomach. 

Mydei’s hand moved to rest gently on Phainon’s chest to ground himself, heart thudding so loudly in his chest. There was familiarity in the way Phainon kissed him—the way his lips felt against his. 

And it was the only kiss Mydei ever wanted to know. 

When they finally pulled apart, just slightly, Phainon’s thumb brushed against Mydei’s cheek. 

“I love you,” Phainon whispered, nudging their noses together. “I always have.”

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 10
chapters.html:
The room was still dim. 

Phainon was still in bed behind him. One arm slung loose around his waist. Their legs were tangled beneath the sheets. Mydei stayed still, eyes open now, adjusting to the pale light streaming in through the windows. 

He wasn’t used to this—having the weight of another person so close. He could feel Phainon’s fingers twitch slightly against his stomach, it was subtle like even in sleep, he didn’t want to let go. 

For a moment, Mydei let himself relax into the touch. 

“What time is it?” Phainon murmured, voice deeper with sleep. 

“Almost five.”

Phainon groaned and nuzzled against his shoulder. “Too early.”

He didn’t move right away. Then, reluctantly, he lifted himself onto one elbow. “I should head out before Augusta wakes.”

Mydei turned slightly to look at him, a little unsure of if he wanted him to go, but he nodded anyway. Phainon’s hair was a little messy and there were faint creases on his cheek from the pillow. He looked cute, Mydei thought. 

Phainon leaned down to press a brief kiss to his cheek before sliding out of bed. 

He grabbed the shirt that had been abandoned on the floor last night and pulled it over his head, then found his pants at the foot of the bed.

Mydei sat up when he did, running his fingers through his hair. 

They took turns in the bathroom. Mydei brushed his teeth while Phainon splashed his face with water, then switched. The house was silent, save for the subtle creak of the floorboards beneath their feet. Augusta’s door was still closed, but Mydei glanced toward it once, just to be sure.

She would be happy. Of course she would be, but he didn’t want to overwhelm her so soon after he’d explained that he and Phainon weren’t together. She was only four and there was only so much change she could take in a year. 

Phainon stretched his arms above his head with a yawn as they made their way downstairs. “I can’t believe you’re up at this hour every morning. The sun’s barely up.”

“The bread doesn’t bake itself,” Mydei rolled his eyes playfully, typing his apron around his waist. He didn’t miss the way Phainon’s eyes followed the movement, but pretended not to notice. “Coffee?” he offered, moving to grab the grounds from the shelf before Phainon could answer. 

Phainon leaned against the counter, arms crossed, watching him with a soft expression. “I was thinking,” he began, “now that we’re dating… does that mean I don’t have to buy bread anymore.”

Mydei snorted. “Who said we’re dating?”

“I—what?” 

“You haven’t taken me out on a proper date,” Mydei said over his shoulder, spreading butter onto a slice of toasted sourdough. 

“Yet,” Phainon murmured, looking up as Mydei handed him a cup of coffee and the bread—warm and soft with a slightly sweet scent to it. 

Mydei sipped his own coffee, hiding the smirk tugging at his lips behind the mug. “Mm. You might still have to pay for bread.”

☼

Mydei had been thinking of hiring someone to help out at the bakery and mornings like this always made him regret not taking the thought seriously. 

He moved behind the counter, reaching for pastries, wrapping up cake orders, and pulling shots of espresso. 

“Two almond croissants and a latte, please,” one of the customers said. 

“One moment,” Mydei replied, sliding a box across the counter to the previous customer. “No, Augusta—”

Too late. She was already in his way again. 

She had been weaving in and out from behind the counter since she’d finished her muffin. At first, it had been cute—little sighs when the bell chimed and it wasn’t him. But now, Mydei had nearly tripped over her for the third time with a warm tray in hand. 

“Mama,” Augusta said insistently, tugging at his apron. “Mama! Is papa coming or not?”

Mydei crouched down quickly, placing a hand on her shoulder. “He said he would. But I need you to sit, okay?”

“But—”

“Augusta,” he said a little more firmly, softening his tone after, “just five more minutes, sweetheart. Sit over there.”

She pouted but dragged her feet to the nearest corner table, climbing into a chair and slumping back. 

Mydei let out a small sigh, but he didn’t have time to dwell on it since someone was already repeating their order. 

Then, finally, the bell chimed again. 

Phainon ducked through the doorway, raising a hand. Before Mydei could say a word, Augusta bolted from her seat. 

“Papa!” she shouted. 

He crouched to catch her, nearly knocked over by the sheer force. “Careful, princess,” he murmured. 

August pulled back from his chest. “You're late..." she pouted. "Were you mad ‘cause I didn’t stay?”

Phainon ran his fingers through her hair, frowning a little. “Of course not, sweetheart. Mama’s easy to miss.” 

"Do you miss mama too?" She asked, tilting her head slightly. 

Phainon caught Mydei's eye, placing a hand on his chest as he nodded solemnly. "Mhm, all the time."

“Buuttt, I cleared my schedule just for you today,” he paused to tap her nose, “and—there’s still one more day left if you want to stay over.”

Augusta’s mouth formed into a little ‘o’, dragging out the sound as she looked back toward Mydei like she was still a little unsure of if she wanted to leave him behind.

Phainon let out a little laugh. “And maybe this time… mama can come too.”

“Really?” she lit up, bouncing on her feet. 

Mydei narrowed his eyes at the two of them. “Maybe,” he said simply, but a smile tugged at his lips. 

☼

Augusta had opened the door before Mydei had the chance to knock twice, her face lighting up as soon as she saw him. She grabbed his hand and tugged him inside like she’d been waiting forever.

“Mama! You came!”

From somewhere deeper in the apartment, Phainon’s voice rang out, “Told you he’d make it! Just in time for dinner too.”

Mydei dropped his overnight bag by the foot of the couch in the living room, taking in the space. Phainon had really made this place home over the past year. 

As Augusta scampered off to her room, Mydei took in his surroundings. There were shelves stacked with rows of books—Phainon’s own little library. Some were old and cracked at the spines, others glossy and new. He smiled to himself when he noticed the bottom shelf lined with a few children’s books. 

In the kitchen, Phainon glanced over his shoulder from the stove, eyes warm. “What do you think?” he asked.  

“It’s…nice,” Mydei settled on, crossing the room to lean against the counter. 

Phainon just smiled as he plated the pasta and reached for the salad bowl. “Go sit. You’re not allowed to lift a finger tonight.”

Mydei didn’t argue, he’d already been run ragged at the bakery, and he could definitely use a break. He pulled out a chair at the table as Augusta joined him too, climbing up on the chair beside him, chattering about how she helped stir the sauce. 

After dinner, they ended up curled together on the couch to watch a move Augusta had picked out. 

Midway through, Augusta’s eyes began to droop as she leaned against the arm rest. “Mama…” she said sleepily, “where are you going to sleep?”

Mydei exchanged a glance with Phainon. 

Phainon leaned forward, scooping her up. “With me. My bed is bigger,” he said gently, standing up as Augusta mumbled something against his shoulder. “Besides, a princess like you deserves her space.”

Augusta giggled a little at that as Phainon kissed the top of her head. “Let’s get you to bed, hm?”

☼

The soft glow from the lamp light softened the edges of Phainon's room. It was neater than Mydei had expected—though he wasn't sure if it was always that way or Phainon had cleaned up because he knew he'd be coming.

Mydei fought the urge to open his closet to see if there was anything stuffed in there. 

Instead, he dropped his overnight bag by the ottoman at the foot of the bed, settling on the comforter. He sat up against the headboard, thinking about pulling out his phone to keep himself occupied—he'd gotten a few orders through emails that he still had to sort through after all. 

He’d heard Phainon’s voice just a few minutes ago as he read to Augusta. He exhaled and let his head fall back slightly, closing his eyes for a moment. This was…strange. He hadn’t slept anywhere but in his own room in a long time.

He let himself settle into the idea of it. Being here more often. Sleeping in the same bed. Waking up next to someone that wasn't four and didn't drool. 

A few more minutes passed before Phainon finally stepped into the room, shutting the door behind him with a soft click . 

“She’s asleep,” he said. “Took three stories, but now I get you all to myself.”

Mydei looked at him, a half-smile tugging at his mouth. “It usually takes me one.”

Phainon gave him a playful eye roll as he reached for the hem of his shirt. “Show-off.”

He pulled the fabric off, letting it fall with a careless toss toward the chair near his desk. Mydei’s gaze followed the movement. “And you have more experience,” he added. 

“Mm…or I’m not as easy to con,” Mydei teased, eyes still tracing the lines of muscle in Phainon’s back and arms. 

He glanced toward him. “My eyes are up here, you know.”

“You know what you’re doing.”

Phainon’s lips curved into a smirk. He walked over, bracing his hands on either side of Mydei as he leaned forward, close enough that their knees brushed. 

“Oh?” his voice was low, “and what exactly am I doing?”

Before Mydei could answer, Phainon pushed him gently back into the pillows, straddling his thighs with all the confidence in the world. Still, Mydei’s hands found his waist, fingertips curling against his skin. 

“Being annoying,” Mydei muttered, even as his mouth tilted up. 

Phainon dipped down to kiss him like he’d been waiting all day to do this. Maybe longer. Mydei melted into it, parting his lips when Phainon’s tongue brushed against them. 

His hand slipped beneath the hem of his shirt, fingertips trailing over his stomach. Mydei inhaled sharply against his mouth, but he didn’t stop him. He just kissed him harder, one arm looping around his shoulders to pull him closer. 

Phainon made a quiet sound into his mouth, and Mydei slid his other hand up his spine, nails grazing lightly. Phainon just barely shivered against the touch. 

He pulled back for a second, a little breathless before he pushed Mydei’s shirt higher, coaxing it over his head in one easy motion and tossing it aside. 

His hand found the small of Mydei’s back, mouth trailing down the line of his jaw to his neck. 

“Didn’t get to say hello properly,” Phainon murmured, teeth skimming over his throat. 

Phainon took his time, teasing with featherlight touches, but Mydei was getting impatient. 

Phainon's voice faltered when Mydei flipped them over in one smooth motion, pushing Phainon into the mattress, his thighs straddling his hips. Phainon blinked up at him, startled for half a second, before something smug lit up his expression. 

“You’ve been holding out on me,” Phainon said, hands coming to rest on Mydei’s bare waist. He inhaled sharply, cursing under his breath when Mydei nipped at the skin below his ear. 

His hands cupped Phainon’s jaw, eyes locking on his. “You talk too much.”

And then his lips were on his again, dragging it out as he rolled his hips down just enough to make Phainon’s breath catch. 

It was almost too easy to get him like this. 

Phainon’s fingers dug harder into his sides. “Mydei…”

“Shut up,” he muttered. 

Phainon barely got the chance to catch a breath before Mydei was kissing him again—more insistent and bruising. 

“Okay,” Phainon breathed, managing a light laugh between kisses. “So you’re in a mood.”

“Phainon,” Mydei warned, fingers grazing along the waistband of his pants and slipping underneath. “I said shut up.”

Before either of them could push any further, a quiet creak cut through the moment.

Both of them froze. Mydei’s hand stilled halfway down, Phainon’s lips parted beneath him. Mydei turned his head, already dreading what he might see.

In the doorway, Augusta was standing with one hand gripping the edge of the frame. Her hair was messy from sleep and her pajama top was crooked. She blinked blearily at them, rubbing one eye.

“Mamaaa…” she whined. “Papa forgot to check for monsters.”

A beat passed. 

Maybe—maybe she hadn’t noticed , Mydei rationalized, holding on to the hope that they hadn't, in fact, traumatized their daughter for life. 

Phainon cleared his throat, voice slightly too high. “Oh. Right.”

Mydei slipped off of him as casually as possible. He yanked the blanket up over his chest as Augusta wandered into the room, completely unbothered. 

They shared a look before Phainon was sitting up and reaching for her. 

“I did forget, huh sweetheart?” he said as he smoothed down her hair. “Let’s go check, okay?”

She leaned into his shoulder as he stood with her in his arms. 

Mydei dragged a hand down his face the moment they turned, mouthing a silent fuck into his palm.

At least she hadn’t asked—

“Why was mama on top of you?” Augusta asked suddenly, lifting her head from Phainon’s shoulder to look between the two of them as if she were trying to piece together an explanation in her mind. 

Mydei pressed a hand over his mouth. 

Phainon didn’t miss a beat. “How about,” he said as he adjusted her in his arms, “we stop talking for a while.”

“But—”

“Shhhh no talking, sweetheart... the monsters might—uh, hear."

Mydei shot him a glare. She was never going back to sleep at this rate.

"Monsters?" Augusta's eyes widened.

Phainon glanced over at him with pleading eyes, mouthing a sorry.

"Papa's just being silly, there aren't any monsters—he'll even check for you," he reassured.

With that, they headed toward the hallway, Phainon whispering softly to her. 

Mydei slumped back into the pillows the second the door closed behind them.

This was definitely going to come back to haunt him. 

Chapter End Notes
