chapters.html:
Mydei stood in front of the vanity, one hand threading through his hair, the other holding a comb that was doing very little except giving him something to fidget with. He had a couple of bobby pins between his lips as he tilted his head, examining the way his hair fell. 

He’d pulled part of his hair back into a half-knot, letting the rest fall in soft layers that framed his face just enough to look effortless, and not like he’d spent the last half hour perfecting it. 

He’d changed into dark slacks and a maroon knit sweater—he’d rolled his sleeves up, then back down, and then back up to his forearms again. He’d decided on wearing two silver rings on one hand with a third resting on his pinky on the other hand. 

It wasn’t that he meant to dress up for Phainon, but he definitely did. 

Mydei wasn’t nervous.  

Not really. 

Maybe a little.

“Mamaaa,” Augusta called from down the hall, where she had been playing with her dolls earlier. She rounded the corner, feet skidding softly on the floor and peeked her head into the bedroom. 

She gasped when she saw him, eyes widening. “You look soooo pretty!”

Mydei pulled the pins from his mouth and looked at her through the mirror. “That’s all you, sweetheart.”

She giggled at that, walking into the room and climbing on to his bed. “Are you going somewhere fancy?” she asked, swinging her feet. 

“Not fancy. Just out.”

She pursed her lips. “With who?”

“A friend,” he replied smoothly, reaching for his cologne. 

“Like a date?”

He paused, arching a brow. “Where’d you hear that from?”

She shrugged. “Is it a date?”

Mydei gave her a sideways glance, letting the question pass without an answer as he sprayed the cologne once and waved the scent off his wrist. But Augusta wasn’t deterred.

“Can papa come watch me then?” she asked, eyes full of hope. “While you’re out.”

Mydei glanced back at her, turning to lean against the vanity. “Ah—not tonight, sweetheart. I think papa’s a little busy with work.”

She frowned. 

He was about to step towards her when the lights flickered. His brows knit together—that definitely wasn’t supposed to happen. He’d even changed the bulbs a couple of days ago.

He brushed it off as a small surge, and then—

Everything went dark. 

The hum of the bathroom fan stopped. A faint thud echoed from the kitchen as the fridge cut out. Mydei stilled, blinking at his own reflection that was only lit by the light creeping in through the windows. 

“Mama?”

He crossed the room and gently ruffled her hair. “It’s okay. Just a power outage. It’ll come back soon.”

But his stomach sank before the words had fully left his mouth. 

The fridge. 

The bakery.

“Shit,” he muttered under his breath. “Shit, shit—”

He grabbed his phone and turned on the flashlight, nearly blinding them both. Augusta made a sound of protest and he mumbled a quick apology, patting her head before tapping out a few messages. 

First to Castorice since she’d agreed to babysit, letting her know that he wouldn’t need her to come over tonight. 

Then to Phainon:

Power is out here. I have to stay

I’m sorry. Raincheck?

He ran a hand down his face, trying to mentally calculate what was in the fridge. 

What could he salvage?

What would spoil first?

He sighed. 

Then looked at Augusta. “Alright,” he said, scooping her up easily. “Ready to be mama’s little helper?”

Augusta grinned, patting her stomach. “I can eat all the cakes.”

He laughed, though a little tiredly. “I don’t think we’re there just yet, sweetheart.”

☼

The bakery lights flickered back to life with a low hum. Mydei stood in the back hallway, his hand still on the circuit breaker, letting out a quiet breath of relief. He could hear Augusta clapping faintly from the front, her voice echoing cheerily: “Mama did it!”

“Mostly,” he muttered to himself, already making his way back to the front. 

But the relief was short-lived. 

The fridge hadn’t turned on. 

He pressed his hand against the side. No vibration. No hum. The digital glow of the temperature display remained dark too. He pulled the door open, checking the fan inside without any luck. 

He clicked the panel, tried to rest it. Still nothing. 

A string of quiet curses tumbled under his breath as he stood back and raked a hand through his hair. The fridge wasn’t coming back on. And with the power out along the entire block, there was no way he would be able to transfer anything elsewhere. 

He looked toward the front. Augusta was seated at one of the tables drawing on a scrap piece of paper with a marker. 

Then back to the kitchen. 

Fine. If the power wasn’t coming back and the fridge was done for the night, then they weren’t going to waste a single thing. 

He moved fast, tying his apron around his waist as he clicked on the rest of the kitchen lights. The registers were out, but he could take notes and tally everything later. 

He wasn’t worried about sales tonight. He just didn’t want anything going in the trash. 

“Hey,” he called out to Augusta. “Want to help me set out some of these pastries?”

“Yes!” Augusta slid off the chair and ran over. 

“We’re opening the bakery,” he said, lifting her over the counter. “Just for a little while.”

Within the hour, the front of the bakery glowed with warm light. Mydei set out a chalkboard sign outside to get people to come in and even had Augusta help him beckon people inside.

People trickled in slowly at first. Some curious neighbours, then passersby grateful for the light and inviting smell of vanilla and sugar. Mydei handed out slices of cake and day-warm pastries, explaining with a smile that the fridge had gone out and they had far too much to eat alone.

It’d started to get busier a little while later, the hum of conversation filling the air along with soft clatter of plates and cups. Mydei moved between the counter and the kitchen, sleeves shoved past his elbows, and his rings long abandoned behind the counter. 

Augusta sat at one of the tables, now making paper crafts with two other kids from the neighbourhood. She waved every time he passed by, which he returned with a quick smile. 

He was grateful. Of course he was. The turnout was beyond anything he’d expected. But keeping track of what had been given out, who wanted what, and what he was supposed to give out first was starting to blur. He hadn’t sat down in two hours. He hadn’t even—

The bell above the door chimed. 

Mydei barely registered it at first.

But then a soft whistle. 

Phainon had stepped inside. His dark coat was slightly damp from the drizzle outside, and his eyes swept the packed space before landing on Mydei. 

“Didn’t know you were throwing a party.”

Mydei fought the urge to smile. “What are you doing here?”

Phainon arched a brow. “Date got cancelled, remember?”

“Right…you didn’t have to—”

“Mydei.”

“Hm?”

“Let me help,” he said simply, and heat immediately rose to Mydei’s cheeks. 

Phainon smirked faintly, leaning forward and dropping his voice. “Tell me where you want me.”

Mydei opened his mouth to object. Or say thank you. Or something. 

But all that came out was: “The fridge is broken.”

Phainon chuckled. “I figured.”

And then without hesitation, he rolled up his sleeves and stepped behind the counter to tie one of the extra aprons around his waist. 

A few heads turned, curious and surprised, but Phainon didn’t seem to mind even as some whispers started. 

“I’ll handle things. Go sit.”

Mydei let out a quiet breath, grabbing a glass of water. 

“Papa!” Augusta’s voice broke through the clatter and noise.

Phainon turned just in time for Augusta to come barreling through. He bent down quickly and caught her, lifting her into his arms like he’d done a thousand times at this point. 

“Hey, babygirl,” he said, kissing her cheek. “Having fun?”

Augusta nodded. “Are you helping Mama too?”

“I am,” he said, adjusting her on his hip, lowering his voice. “I have to snag a brownie somehow.”

Augusta giggled at that, then pulled something from her pocket: a lollipop with a slightly crumpled wrapper. “Look! I saved you this. This one is mama’s favourite!”

Phainon took it from her with a soft smile. “Thank you, sweetheart,” he said, already unwrapping it and popping it into his mouth. Augusta wriggled slightly in his grip and he set her down on her feet.

She was about to scamper off when she paused, turning to tug on his sleeve. “Are you going to sleepover?” She asked as if to make sure she’d see him later. 

“If Mama’s okay with it.”

Mydei gave her a faint nod from where he was sitting on a stool behind the counter. Augusta beamed brightly before she was dashing back to where her friends were sitting. 

“You’re getting bold.”

“It makes her happy,” Phainon said without hesitation, pulling the lollipop out of his mouth. He glanced over the counter before leaning down to meet Mydei’s eye. His fingers brushed over his jaw, tilting his chin towards him. It was soft, just a press of lips, But Mydei could taste the faint flavour of cherry on his lips. 

When they parted, Mydei was already preparing to scold him for being careless. Anyone could’ve seen them. Especially their daughter. 

“Phai—mmph.” he began, but before he could get the words out, Phainon was shoving the lollipop into his mouth. 

Mydei just stared at him. “What’s wrong with you?”

“She said it was your favourite.”

Mydei averted his gaze. “...She’s not wrong,” he muttered around the candy. 

☼

The bakery had quieted around midnight, though a few people still lingered outside by the stoop, sharing laughter under the dim moonlight.

Phainon had taken Augusta to bed with a determined glint in his eye and a quiet “watch me crush bedtime tonight.” Mydei had only chuckled, silently hoping that they wouldn’t have a repeat of what happened the last time he’d put Augusta to bed. 

Mydei wiped down the counter absentmindedly, his body aching from hours of running on adrenaline alone. 

The soft creak of the door drew his attention. 

A man stepped inside, He was tall, broad-shouldered with brown hair. His eyes were a little tired, but he smiled kindly at him. Mydei straightened a little, brushing his hands off on a towel.

“Sorry,” he began, “we’re out for the night—”

“Augusta’s yours, right?” he asked. 

Mydei nodded, caught off guard. “Yeah. I’m Mydei.” 

The man offered a hand. “Marcus. I’m Serena’s dad. She’s in Augusta’s class. I’ve heard your name a few times and figured I’d stop by since you were open. Cassondra mentioned you run this place. Thought I’d check it out.”

There was something in his voice that felt like he’d rehearsed this in the car before coming in.

Mydei shook his hand briefly. “Ah, right. I don’t believe we’ve met before?”

“Didn’t make it to the fall open house” Marcus replied. “Divorce stuff. You know how it is.”

Mydei offered a polite smile. “I’m sorry to hear that.”

Marcus leaned a little on the counter, eyes sweeping across the bakery. “This place is beautiful.” Then, almost as an afterthought: “It must be a lot. Running a business and raising a four year old.”

“It’s… manageable,” Mydei said, unsure if this was going where he thought it was.

“Well, you make it look effortless,” he replied, his gaze lingering longer than it should have. He reached out, his hand brushing Mydei’s arm—a touch that was just a little too familiar to be friendly. “Honestly, it looks good on you.”

Mydei’s mouth twitched. He didn’t pull away, but he didn’t lean into either. This wasn’t the first time someone had tried this. Ever since Augusta had started school and word had gotten out about the handsome young single mother, there had been a steady stream of “drop-ins”—it got him more customers so he wasn’t one to complain. 

But things weren’t exactly the same now.

And right on cue, the stairs behind them creaked. 

“I think I’m getting better at this,” Phainon called out, sounding way too pleased with himself. “I got her down in two stories this time and I didn’t even have to bribe her with golden honeycakes for breakfast.”

He emerged from the stairwell, hair slightly tousled, looking both exhausted and smug. “And I checked for mon—”

His voice trailed off when his eyes landed on Marcus. 

Then the hand on Mydei’s arm. 

The shift in his expression was so small that anyone else might have missed it. His mouth pressed into a thin line as he straightened. He crossed the room in a few easy steps and draped an arm around Mydei’s shoulders.

“What’s going on here, hm?” he asked, tone a little too sweet. 

“I was just telling Mydei—”

“It’s Mydeimos," Phainon muttered, earning him a light kick on the shin from Mydei and a muttered “Phai.”

Marcus cleared his throat. “I was just saying that the place looks great. I’m Marcus. You must be a friend?”

“Phainon,” he responded, a little firm but not exactly unkind. “Augusta’s father.”

Marcus paused, looking between the two of them like he wasn’t expecting anyone to be here tonight with Mydei. He rubbed the back of his head sheepishly. “Ah well, I see,” he began. “I’ll get out of your hair then.”

He turned and made his way to the door, the bell chiming gently as he stepped out into the night. 

Mydei turned slowly, still tucked under Phainon’s arm. “Mydeimos? Really?”

“You don’t like your full name anymore?” 

Mydei shook his head, pulling away to lean back against the counter. “You,” he poked a finger to his chest, “are a jealous, jealous man.”

Phainon placed a hand on his chest, failing to hide the smirk tugging at his lips. “Me? Never.” 

☼

They’d already brushed their teeth and gotten ready for bed in their usual sleep clothes—Mydei in a loose tank top and Phainon without his shirt.

Mydei had slipped under the covers first, curling onto his side with a sigh. The day had been long and he was ready to just sleep. He was already halfway there when he felt the mattress dip behind him.

Then came a sigh.

Then another one. Louder this time, exaggerated and definitely performative.

Mydei didn’t bother opening his eyes. “Are you done?”

“No.”

“Are you going to be?”

Phainon paused for a beat. Then his arm wrapped around Mydei’s waist, followed by a grumble pressed right against his nape.

“He was so not your type.”

Mydei laughed quietly into the pillow. “Phainon…”

“I’m just saying,” he murmured, pulling him closer. “Who even flirts with someone so brazenly like that anyway? It’s embarrassing.”

“I recall you doing that.”

“Marcus,” Phainon scoffed, dismissing Mydei’s comment. “What a stupid name. It’s a stupid name.”

“Are you pouting?”

“No.”

Mydei turned, shifting slightly so he could see him. And yes, Phainon was very clearly pouting, lower lip pushed out and brows furrowed in a way that reminded him of Augusta. 

He reached out, and gently brushed a few strands of hair back from his forehead. “You know I only have room for one idiot in my life.”

Phainon narrowed his eyes, frowning. “So you think I’m an idiot.”

Mydei smiled, shaking his head. “Come here, you big baby.”

Phainon didn’t need more encouragement than that, practically melting into his arms. Mydei’s hand found his hair without thinking, scratching lightly as Phainon hummed.

They stayed like that for a few moments, just basking in the silence and each other’s presence. 

“I’m going to say this once, so you better be listening,” Mydei spoke softly. 

“Hm?” Phainon blinked up at him, pushing himself up on one elbow. 

“I don’t say it often, but…I love you.” 

Phainon looked like he could barely hold back a grin, expression immediately softening. 

He didn’t say anything. He just leaned down and kissed him slowly, smiling against his lips. He pulled back for just a moment, bumping noses before pressing their lips together again, deeper this time, a hand sliding up to cup Mydei’s jaw.

When they broke apart, he hesitated for a moment. 

“Something on your mind?” Mydei asked lightly. 

“I want to tell her.”

chapters.title: Chapter 12
chapters.html:
The bedroom was quiet save for the soft hum of traffic outside and the distant sound of a siren making its way down the street. 

It had been one of those days that had passed by in a blur. Mydei’s muscles ached from the weight of it. 

He’d spent hours behind the counter, piping frosting, portioning out dough, and rotating trays in the oven. It’d gotten a lot busier lately, customers coming in with requests for weddings, graduation parties, baby showers, or just ordering sweets for reasons they barely bothered to explain. Some lingered for coffee, others for conversation. 

Still, he'd smiled through it all, but the moment Augusta was down for the night, his body nearly collapsed into the mattress. 

His hair was still damp from a hasty shower earlier, and he exhaled slowly, letting himself melt into the sheets. The ache in his shoulders would settle by morning, but the ache behind his ribs… maybe not. 

Something was missing.

His phone had buzzed earlier when he was cleaning up. Phainon had sent him a photo of a sad looking muffin squished on a napkin with the message: 

not as good as yours :( 

Mydei had rolled his eyes fondly, smiling softly. Phainon had been working longer days with back to back meetings, so they hadn’t seen much of each other. 

He missed him. 

Really missed him. 

The kind of missing that Mydei never thought he’d feel again. The kind that made him turn toward the empty half of the bed without even realizing. It was strange how Phainon had become such a constant not only in Augusta’s life—but Mydei’s too. 

He sighed, closed his eyes, and let his body start to drift. 

He was halfway there when he heard it. The soft shuffling of little feet across the hardwood floor. 

“Mama…”

Augusta’s voice was hushed and sleepy. Mydei opened one eye to see her hovering in the doorway, clutching Fig Stew in her arms. Her cheeks were flushed, her lip wobbling just slightly.

He didn’t ask. He didn’t need to. With a quiet hum, he lifted the blanket and made space for her. 

She climbed in without hesitation, tucking herself against his side. He pulled the covers over both of them, smoothing down her hair. 

“Did you have a bad dream, little one?” he asked softly, pressing a kiss to the top of her head. 

She nodded against his chest, silent at first as her fingers curled into the fabric of his shirt. “Will you stay awake until I fall asleep?” 

“Mhm,” he reassured, rubbing little circles on her back. “You’re safe with Mama, sweetheart.” 

Augusta relaxed under his touch, eyes beginning to droop as her breathing evened out. He was almost certain she was asleep. 

Then she whispered, “What if Papa leaves again?”

The words were soft, barely there, but they still made Mydei’s breath catch. 

He pulled her closer. 

“What makes you say that, sweetheart?”

Augusta tilted her head up to look at him. “Papa didn’t come yesterday. He always comes on Fridays.”

Mydei’s chest tightened. She’d gotten used to their routine too by now. 

“He wanted to,” he said gently. “He’s just been busy these last few days, but that doesn’t mean he doesn’t want to see you.”

“But what if he has to go far away again?”

The ache deepened. Mydei had been so wrapped up in how he felt about telling her the truth and whether or not that would overwhelm her that he hadn’t even stopped to think what keeping the secret was doing to her. 

“He’s not going anywhere,” Mydei reassured. It was a promise. “He loves you. So much. And if it were up to him, he’d be here everyday.”

Augusta stayed quiet for a few moments, curling further into him until her head was just below his chin. 

He rubbed her back slowly, mind drifting back to what Phainon had said just a few nights ago. 

“I want to tell her.”

He hadn’t agreed exactly then. He’d only nodded, still a little uncertain. But maybe Phainon was right. 

Maybe it was time. 

Mydei pressed a kiss to Augusta’s forehead before leaning over her to grab his phone. 

“How about we call Papa, hm?” he asked. 

Her eyes lit up. “Can we?”

Mydei chuckled, already dialing Phainon’s number. “Of course we can.”

☼

Mydei had closed the bakery for the day after spending the morning catching up on orders. With the wedding coming up, he didn’t want to bite off more than he could chew.  

Phainon had also texted that he had the day off, so he thought it would be good for the three of them to do something together that didn’t involve staying home. 

The park was lively with chatter, dogs barking and children playing. It was one of the nicer days of the season—just cool enough that the breeze felt like a gentle push against their backs as they walked. 

Augusta giggled, running a few paces ahead of them, spinning around under the canopy of trees. She was wearing her favourite overalls with blue flowers and her sneakers were already scuffed with grass stains. 

Phainon stretched his arms overhead with a small groan, looking up at the sky. “Feels good to be out.” 

“Mm, you’ve been stuck in your office all week,” Mydei hummed as shifted the picnic basket in his hand to the other arm. Then, he leaned into Phainon to drop his voice. “I think we should tell her tonight.”

Phainon stopped in his tracks, gaze drifting to Augusta. “You’re sure?”

He nodded. “We can’t exactly keep it from her forever.”

Phainon just grinned, bumping their shoulders together. “Tonight,” he echoed the sentiment.

He leaned in a little for what seemed like was a kiss, but Mydei turned his face just in time and used two fingers to flick his forehead. 

“Ow!” Phainon gasped, clutching his chest as if he’d been mortally wounded. “What was that for?!” 

“Wait until our daughter knows, lover boy.”

Before Phainon could launch into whatever dramatic speech he had prepared, Augusta’s voice broke through the air. 

“Mama! Papa!” she called out, hurrying back over to them. She grabbed both of their hands, tugging them towards the grass. “I found a good spot!”

They shared a fond look as they made their way to a patch of grass just below a tall tree. Mydei got to spreading out the blanket as Phainon helped unload the basket. They’d definitely had too much. He’d packed an array of sandwiches, fruit slices, a small tin of cookies, and a thermos of iced peach tea. 

Augusta had abandoned them to run around in circles after a butterfly, but eventually flopped down in Phainon’s lap once everything was set up. He grunted a little from the force, letting out an “oof” that made her giggle. 

“I’m gonna eat four sandwiches,” she declared.

Mydei chuckled, unwrapping one half and handed it to her. “How about we start with one?”

They ate slowly, stretched out on the blanket together, and something blossomed in Mydei’s chest at the comfort of it all.

“You’ve really outdone yourself, ba—De,” Phainon caught himself in time, a faint heat rising to his cheeks. 

Augusta furrowed her brows at the slip-up, chewing thoughtfully. “Why did you call Mama a baddie?” she frowned. “Mama isn’t bad.” 

“Oh that’s—uh, I didn’t mean—” he stumbled over the words. “It means he’s pre—mmph!” 

Mydei reached to clamp a hand over his mouth before he did irreparable damage to their daughter’s vocabulary, shooting him a glare. “That’s just Papa being silly, you know how he is,” he brushed off. 

“Papa,” Augusta said solemnly. 

“Yes, sweetheart?” His voice was muffled by Mydei’s palm, but he retracted his hand. 

“You shouldn’t be silly all the time,” she said before dropping her voice to a whisper, cupping a hand around her mouth. “Or Mama might send you to time-out and then you can’t play with me.” 

He huffed a little laugh, adjusting her bucket hat slightly before placing a hand on his chest. “I’ll keep that in mind.” 

Mydei tried to stifle a laugh as Augusta clapped her hands like the matter was settled. 

It wasn’t long before she was back on her feet and tugging on Phainon’s arm, pointing to the playground. 

Papa, can you push me on the swings now?” 

“Alright, alright,” Phainon said. “I’m…” he trailed off, glancing over at Mydei as if he were gauging how much trouble he’d be in if he didn’t help with clean up. “I’ll be right there.”

Augusta frowned.

“Go ahead, I got it here,” Mydei playfully rolled his eyes. “Just not too high,” he added, giving both of them a pointed look. 

“She likes going high—” 

“And what happened last time?”

Phainon laughed sheepishly as he stood, scooping Augusta easily into his arms. “We’ll be responsible, Mama,” he said before running off with Augusta toward the play structures.

☼

Mydei stepped out of the bathroom, towel slung around his shoulders, the faint scent of jasmine and honey soap still lingered on his skin. His hair was damp, clinging slightly to his forehead as he ran a hand through it on the way to Augusta’s room.

The door was open and Augusta was sitting on the floor in her pajamas, happily chatting away about something that happened at school.

Phainon was sitting behind her on a beanbag chair. He was listening in the way he always did with her like nothing else mattered in the world even if he’d heard the story countless times already. His expression was soft as he ran a comb through her hair gently. 

Mydei paused by the doorway. 

He didn’t say anything right away. Just stood there watching them fondly. 

It wasn’t anything grand, but Mydei couldn’t help but think that this is what their lives could look like if they stopped waiting for the right time to name it. 

Augusta kept talking, oblivious, and Phainon smiled as he replied with a gentle, “Mhm? Then what happened?”

Phainon looked up after a moment, sensing him there, and their eyes locked. 

Mydei nodded. 

He stepped into the room and gently lifted Augusta, earning a soft squeak of laughter from her. She looped her arms around his neck briefly before he settled her into bed, tucking the blankets around her. 

Phainon climbed up onto the mattress on one side while Mydei settled on the other. 

“There’s something we want to talk to you about,” Mydei said gently, brushing her hair out of her eyes. 

Augusta blinked up at him, a little curious. “Am I in trouble?” she asked. 

Phainon shook his head. “My girl? never.”

Augusta looked between them, slightly more alert now. “Are—are you going far away again?”

“No, no,” Phainon said quickly, resting a hand on her stomach. “It’s about us. Mama and I.”

Mydei gave Phainon a glance before letting him take the lead. “You know how I love spending time with you and Mama, right?”

She nodded. 

“And we’ve been spending a lot of time together,” Mydei continued. “Not just as your Papa and Mama, but… as something more too.”

Augusta blinked. “Like… Papa is your boyfriend?” she asked, eyes wide with realization. 

Phainon laughed softly and leaned in to kiss her cheek with an exaggerated ‘mwah,’ making her squirm under the covers. “Yes, exactly.”

“Papa!” she giggled, shoving at him playfully. “Too many kisses!”

“There’s no such thing!” Phainon teased, pressing one more to her temple before pulling back. 

Augusta was still after that, eyes starting to droop—the park had definitely tuckered her out. Her fingers curled around the edge of the blanket as she took it all in. Then, she yawned, and turned toward Mydei, hand searching for his. 

He smiled softly when her hand curled into his, tucking a strand of loose hair behind her ear. It was tied off a little lopsided, but Phainon was improving. 

“Hey…” he murmured, eyes flicking up to meet Phainon’s. “You think you could give us a minute?”

Phainon hesitated, but he nodded anyway. He leaned over to kiss Augusta’s forehead first then moved to press a kiss against Mydei’s temple. He lingered there for a second before pulling away.

“I’ll be just outside,” he said softly.

When he was gone, Mydei leaned down to rest his head beside Augusta’s. She smiled sleepily, and turned to face him.

“Are you going to tell me a secret?” she whispered. 

“Mmm, not much of a secret,” he said. “But something just for you and me.”

She scooted a little closer.

“I love you more than anything, and I don’t want you to be scared or nervous to ask me anything, okay?”

“I know,” she whispered, nuzzling against his shoulder. “I love you too, Mama.”

Mydei smiled, and brought up a hand to cradle the back of her head.

 “Do you love Papa?” she asked after a moment.

Mydei nodded. “I do.”

“Does Papa love you?” 

“He does. Maybe a little too much.” 

Augusta pursed her lips, brows pinching together. “Then…are we going to live together?”

“Maybe one day,” he said, brushing his thumb along her cheek. “For now, we can stick to sleepovers and breakfast together.”

“I like when Papa stays.”

“Yeah,” he whispered. “Me too.”

A pause. 

“Will we finally get another baby?”

Mydei laughed softly, pressing his forehead to hers. “We’ll see about that one.”

She giggled and slowly closed her eyes. “Okay…”

He stayed there for a long while. When her grip on his hand loosened, he finally pulled away, just enough to slip out from under the blankets. He paused at the door, looking back at her one more time. 

Then he stepped into the hallway, where Phainon was waiting. 

He pushed off of the wall as their eyes met. 

And without a word, Mydei reached for his hand.

☼

The morning light spilled through the curtains of the bedroom. Mydei was the first to stir, shifting under the blanket but he didn’t open his eyes. Phainon’s arm was draped loosely around his waist, their legs tangled beneath the sheets. 

Mydei felt lighter now that the weight of the secret had been lifted from his shoulders. 

He was just about to shift closer to Phainon when the sound of footsteps approached. 

Then—

“Mama!” Augusta chirped as she scrambled over to them, clambering over Phainon to wedge herself between them. “Are you awake?” 

Mydei cracked one eye open, laughing sleepily. “You’re up early, sweetheart.” 

Augusta just wriggled under the covers until she was tucked into Mydei’s side and grinned up at him. “I wanted to cuddle with you, Mama.”

Phainon, who had been startled awake by a knee to the stomach, blinked groggily. “What about me?” he mumbled. “Don’t I get cuddles?” 

“I like Mama’s cuddles.” 

“Ohhh” he groaned dramatically, flopping onto his back and throwing an arm over his face. “Betrayed by my own flesh and blood.”

Mydei smirked, leaning in to kiss the side of Augusta’s head. “That’s my girl.” 

“Don’t encourage this.” 

“Mama gives better cuddles!” Augusta giggled mischievously. 

Phainon huffed, but then reached across their daughter and wrapped arm around both of them to pull them close. “Fine, then I’ll just have to cuddle both of you. You can’t escape now.” 

Augusta shrieked. “Papa, you always squish me!” 

“That’s the price of betrayal, babygirl,” Phainon declared, kissing her cheek. 

Mydei chuckled again, patting down Augusta’s hair—her braids had come a little loose from sleep. “How about breakfast, hm?” 

“No plans today,” Phainon murmured, his voice softer as he leaned in to kiss Mydei’s cheek. “Let’s stay like this for a little while.” 

Augusta gasped, hands clasping over her mouth immediately, eyes going wide. “Papa kissed Mama~” she said in a sing-song voice. 

Phainon huffed a small laugh, then looked back at Mydei and this time leaned in for a proper kiss on the lips. 

Augusted scrunched up her face, frowning. 

“Ewww!” She cried, pulling the blanket over her head. “Yuck!” 

Phainon shared a look with Mydei. 

“I’m never doing that!” Came Augusta’s muffled voice from beneath the covers. “I’m only going to ever kiss Mama and Papa.” 

Phainon peeled back the blanket to get a look at her face, nodding solemnly. “I’m fine with that.” 

Augusta looked between them suspiciously. “You won’t do it again, right?” 

Phainon smirked, leaning into Mydei as if he was going to. 

“Papa!” 

“Alright, alright,” he said. “No more kissing, little one.” 

Augusta let out a little content sigh—probably still a little sleepy. She shifted so she was closer to Phainon. 

“Papa…” her voice trailed off as she yawned. “You should stay forever. It’s fun when you’re here.” 

Phainon’s expression softened, eyes flicking up to meet Mydei’s. “I’m not going anywhere,” he whispered softly as Mydei reached for his hand wordlessly to lace their fingers together. 

“I’m home.”

“Okay! Papa, you go stand there,” Augusta instructed, pointing to the far end of the hallway near the living room. ‘And Mama, you go over here and you have to look surprised!”

It was early evening, and they had just gotten done with dinner. Phainon had just come over after work along with Castorice and Cipher. They were still lounging in the living room, halfway through a game of cards when Augusta had insisted on practicing her flower girl routine for the wedding. 

Phainon bit back a grin and exchanged a look with Mydei. 

“Shouldn’t auntie Cas be the one walking down the aisle?” Mydei asked.

Augusta narrowed her eyes. “Mama,” she said, hands on her hips. “Auntie Cas has to save it for the real wedding. Now go! Go go go!”

“She makes a good point, little prince~” Cipher added as Castorice hummed in agreement. 

Phainon moved into position at the far end of the hallway, near the living room, where Castorice was now sitting cross-legged on the floor. 

Mydei moved to the opposite end, where Cipher was snickering. 

She was dressed in one of her dresses with a pink sash tied in a bow at the back, and she held a small wicker basket filled with crumpled tissues that she wanted to use like real petals. 

“Okay,” Augusta said, positioning herself by Cipher and Mydei. “Everyone ready?”

“Ready,” Castorice gave her a thumbs up from across the room as Cipher nudged her forward slightly. 

Augusta began walking down the hallway, tossing her tissue petals with flair as she hummed the wedding march under her breath. Her brows were furrowed in concentration as she dropped a tissue every couple of steps.

Phainon pretended to tear up, dabbing at his eyes with the edge of his shirt. “She’s so grown up,” he whispered. “Our baby..”

“Papa!” Augusta hissed. “This is serious.”

“Sorry, sorry,” Phainon held up his hands. 

Mydei bit the inside of his cheek to stifle a laugh. “You’re doing amazing, sweetheart,” he said softly as she continued throwing a tissue petal. 

She reached the end of the hallway and did a little spin, tossing one final handful. She turned to Castorice as if she were waiting for her applause. 

“Perfect,” Cas giggled, plucking a makeshift petal out of her own hair, pulling Augusta to sit in her lap. 

“Now Mama walks down,” Augusta said firmly. “You have to smile really big when he does it, Papa!”

Mydei sighed, already resigned, but there was a softness in every step as he walked down the hallway toward them. Augusta clapped her hands and turned to peer up at Phainon. “Look how pretty Mama is!”

Phainon gave a dramatic sigh. “Stunning. The prettiest I’ve ever seen.”

Cipher let out a low whistle. “Hey little one~ don’t you think Mama deserves a veil?”

Augusta gasped, eyes lighting up. 

“Too bad we don’t have one,” Mydei muttered, already sensing what was coming. 

“Don’t you still have that one from the halloween costume?” Castorice pointed out. 

“I know where it is!” Augusta chirped, already back on her feet. Cipher stood with a little too much eagerness, following after her. 

The second her footsteps faded down the hall, Phainon took the opportunity to reach for Mydei. He slipped an arm around his waist and tugged until his forehead was against Mydei’s. “Alone at last,” he murmured, lips already brushing the corner of Mydei’s mouth. “I’m gonna need to hear more about this costume.”

“Mm, not a chance” Mydei hummed, his hands coming to rest loosely on Phainon’s shoulders. The kiss he pressed to Mydei’s lip was soft and familiar, the kind they rarely got away with uninterrupted anymore. 

Castorice cleared her throat loudly from her spot on the floor. “Still here, by the way,” she said. 

Phainon didn’t bother glancing over. “Please, you love this.”

Castorice opened her mouth to argue, but decided against it. Mydei leaned back only slightly, his thumb brushing along Phainon’s jaw. “If she catches us kissing, you know she’s going to say ‘ew.’”

Phainon sighed. “She says that every time. It’s a rite of passage now.”

“We’re back!” Augusta called. She and Cipher rounded the corner with not only the veil but the entire costume. “Mama, you have to put it all on!”

Phainon stepped back slightly, clearly a little too excited as Mydei side-eyed him. 

“Time to dress up~” Cipher grinned, bumping her shoulder against Phainon before winking at him. “You’re welcome,” she whispered.

☼ 

The place had quieted, the only sound remaining the soft hum of the night. 

Mydei was already tugging his shirt off as he padded toward the bed. Phainon was sitting upright against the pillows, eyes fixed on him. “You know,” he started a little too casually. “About that dress—”

“No,” Mydei said instantly without even glancing. 

Phainon gave a wounded little sigh. “I didn’t even finish the sentence.”

“You didn’t have to,” Mydei slid under the covers, tugging the blanket up. “You only want me to put it on so you can take it off.”

Phainon didn’t deny it. He tilted his head, watching Mydei settle in. “That’s not the only reason,” he said, reaching over to brush his fingers down Mydei’s arm. 

Mydei let his eyes close, unbothered. “Still not putting it on.”

“Come on,” Phainon drawled, sliding closer. “Just for a second. I’ll behave.”

“You never behave,” Mydei murmured against the pillow, though a smile tugged at his lips despite himself. 

Phainon flopped onto his side with a dramatic groan and buried his face in Mydei’s shoulder. “You’re so mean to me.”

“I’m not the one trying to seduce someone who just spent an hour putting a child to bed,” Mydei said dryly, but his hand found the back of Phainon’s neck anyway, fingertips gentle as they tangled into his hair. 

Phainon tilted his head to kiss the edge of his collarbone. There was quiet for a few breaths, then Mydei sighed, eyes still closed. “Go to sleep, Phai.”

Then—

“Maybe.”

Phainon just curled up around him, knowing better than to say anything further. 

☼

The wedding was only hours away, but somehow the energy in the bridal suite was calm. Castorice stood in front of the full-length mirror, smoothing her hands down the delicate lace bodice of her dress.

Augusta was sitting on the plush rug nearby, tossing the petals from her basket into the air like confetti. 

“You’re not supposed to throw them yet,” Mydei reminded gently, kneeling down beside her with a small pair of embroidery scissors to fix a stray thread on the ribbon around her basket. 

“I’m practicing,” she replied, watching a petal land in her lap. 

“I think you’ve practiced enough, sweetheart,” Mydei chuckled, brushing a few petals out of her hairs. “At this rate, you won’t have any left for the aisle.”

Augusta’s eyes widened as she gasped, scrambling to pick up the stray petals. Mydei stood, dusting off his slacks as he crossed the room over to Castorice. She smiled at him through the mirror. 

“Ready?” he asked, grabbing her veil to pin to hair. 

She took in a breath before giving a firm nod, hand curling up to her chest. “I can’t believe it’s finally happening. It’s all really… coming together.”

“I told you it would,” Mydei responded, stepping back and tilting his head. 

Castorice turned toward him. She took one step forward. 

And then—

There was a sharp rrrpp.

Castorice stopped mid-step, her eyes wide. “...What was that?”

“Uh-oh,” Augusta gasped, slapping her hands over her mouth. 

She turned just enough to see the damage in the mirror. The fabric below had caught under one of the chairs and split open—albeit not too high, but enough to be noticeable. 

“No no no,” she groaned. “This can’t be happening. There’s not enough—”

“Cas,” Mydei cut in. “Take a deep breath. We can fix this.”

Before she could say anything further, he was already rummaging through the drawers for the sewing kit he’d seen stashed in the room. 

Castorice closed her eyes, taking in a breath before she braced her hands on the back of a nearby chair. Mydei crouched down behind her with the sewing kit. 

Behind them, Augusta crept over, watching silently as he worked. 

“Is it bad?” Castorice asked. 

“It’s fine,” Mydei reassured, eyes darting over to the clock for a moment. “Hey… sweetheart, it’s almost time for the ceremony. Why don’t you go find Papa?”

“‘Kay!” Augusta chirped, already scampering off while mumbling ‘I’m gonna tell Papa what happened.’

Mydei smiled, shaking his head as he continued working on the dress. 

Another few stitches. A final knot, and Mydei sat back on his heels. 

“Done,” he said, patting the fabric. 

Castorice turned slowly, checking the seam in the mirror. “You’re amazing.”

“I know,” Mydei smiled as he stood, extending a hand. “Now, let’s get you down that aisle.”

☼ 

The ceremony was moments away from starting. 

The guests had been seated and the air hummed with excitement as the music started. 

Mydei found Augusta clinging nervously to Phainon’s pant leg. There was a small frown on her face and she held onto her basket of petals like her life depended on it. 

“There you are,” Mydei said, gently crouching down beside. “Hey sweetheart.”

Augusta looked at him with wide eyes. “Mama, I don’t think I can do it.”

Mydei’s eyes softened. “Why not?”

“What if I trip?” she whispered. “Or throw the petals in someone’s face?”

Phainon knelt down with Mydei, resting a hand lightly on her shoulder. “We’ve practiced, haven’t we?”

“But there’s so many people,” she said, voice cracking just a little. 

Behind them, Castorice appeared with her hand in through her sister, Polyxia’s. The two of them stayed back for a moment as Mydei gave them an apologetic look. Polyxia offered a quiet smile, while Castorice stepped forward. 

“Hey,” she said softly, adjusting her dress to crouch down to Augusta’s level. “You know, I’m really nervous too.”

“You are?” Augusta blinked. 

Castorice huffed a laugh. “Of course I am. But you don’t have to be perfect, sweetheart.”

“And we’ll be right there at the end of the aisle. Just walk toward us, okay? Pretend no one else is even there,” Phainon added. 

Augusta looked between all three of them. Her grip loosened slightly on the basket, and she gave a small, shaky nod. 

“Okay,” she murmured. “I can do it.”

Mydei kissed her forehead and stood. “That’s my girl.”

Castorice stood next, smoothing down her newly-mended gown—careful not to get it caught in anything. “Looks like we’re all set now.”

Polyxia offered her sister her arm as Mydei and Phainon made their way down the service corridor. 

They’d just rounded the corner when Phainon slowed to a stop. Mydei turned, confused until Phainon caught him by the wrist and tugged him gently into the side hallway. 

“Phai—” Mydei started, glancing back toward the sound of music swelling faintly from the main hall, “we’re going to miss it—”

“We have time,” Phainon murmured, pulling him close. 

Before Mydei could protest, Phainon’s lips were already on his—firm, greedy with just the right amount of softness. His hands settled at Mydei’s waist, fingertips digging into his sides like he didn’t want to let go. 

“I haven’t seen you all day,” he mumbled against Mydei’s lips, a little breathless. “You’ve been running around like a wedding sprite and I’ve been stuck smiling at everyone.”

Mydei laughed fondly despite himself and Phainon grinned, kissing the edge of his jaw. 

“Phai,” Mydei warned, gently pushing at his chest, though he didn’t exactly move away. “We’re going to miss Augusta’s cue.”

As if on cue, the music shifted into the first notes of the processional. 

“Shit,” Phainon breathed. 

They pulled apart at once and rushed down the hallway. Mydei adjusted his collar as Phainon smoothed his hair as they rounded the final corner. One of the ushers looked vaguely startled, but held the door open just in time for them to slip inside. 

Augusta had just stepped into view at the start of the aisle. She looked serious, still a little nervous, but determined. 

Phainon and Mydei barely made it to their seats when she took the first step forward. Mydei looked toward Cipher. Her eyes locked with his and she raised an eyebrow. He averted his gaze, ignoring the heat rising to his cheeks. 

Phainon reached over to lace their fingers together on Mydei’s knee and Mydei leaned into him as they watched their daughter. 

She walked carefully as she tossed a handfuls of petals from her basket, and the guests let out sighs of affection. Halfway down, her eyes landed on Mydei and Phainon in their seats. She gave them a soft smile as Mydei waved and Phainon flashed a thumbs up. 

Cipher beckoned her forward as she continued. Once she reached the end of the aisle, she quickly made her way over to Mydei and Phainon. Phainon lifted her into his lap as a new swell of music began and all eyes turned toward the archway. 

Castorice appeared with Polyxia by her side. Cipher visibly sucked in a breath at the sight of her, blinking a few times too fast as if she couldn’t believe they’d finally made it to this day. 

When Castorice finally reached the altar, she bent slightly to let Polyxia kiss her cheek, giving her sister’s hand one final squeeze. She mouthed something to Cipher that was too quiet to hear. 

Cipher smiled, expression softening and took her hands. 

The officiant cleared his throat. “Welcome, everyone,” he began. “Today we are gathered to celebrate Castorice and Cipher, in love, in trust, and in the presence of those dearest to them…”

☼ 

The reception was well underway now, the air was warm with laughter as the evening slipped into night. Plates clinked, honey brew flowed freely, and a few guests had already started to dance. 

Mydei stood near one of the tables, sipping a glass of sparkling water and watching Augusta laugh with Polyxia as she twirled the little girl around. Cipher and Cas were caught up in their own conversation, laughing and smiling. The weight of the day had melted into something softer. There had been a few slip-ups, but it was a perfect day. 

Phainon appeared in front of him, extending a hand out. “Dance with me.”

Mydei gave him a skeptical look, but took his hand anyway, letting Phainon pull him gently toward the middle of the dance floor. The music was slow, played by a string quartet. 

Phainon’s hands found his waist as Mydei moved to rest one hand against Phainon’s chest. “You’ve been waiting for this all night.”

“Can you blame me?” Phainon replied. “You rarely let me dance with you.”

Mydei chuckled, letting him take the lead. He rocked them gently in time with the music. 

“Is this really the best you can do?” Mydei teased. 

Phainon pushed out his bottom lip. “Hey, come on, at least I’m not stepping on your toes.”

Mydei sighed. “The bar really is low, isn't it?” he shook his head fondly, looping his arms around Phainon’s neck. He tilted his head slightly, leaning in to kiss him. Somewhere in the distance Cipher shouted about the bouquet toss about to happen. 

But it didn’t matter. Mydei pulled back from Phainon, a little breathless. He felt tears prick at the back of his eyes. He opened his mouth to speak, but no words came out. 

“Hey…” Phainon spoke softly, fingertips tracing the edge of his jaw. “what is it?”

“Thank you,” Mydei whispered, closing his eyes and resting his forehead against Phainon’s. 

“Hm? What for?” 

“For giving me a second chance. For not holding it against me. For showing up for her even when things weren’t perfect.”

Phainon didn’t say anything, he just tilted his head, leaning forward. His lips ghosted over Mydei’s before he pressed them together. His hand trailed to the back of his neck to deepen the kiss, and it spoke louder than any words could ever. 

“You never have to thank me for that,” Phainon whispered, inches from his face. “I love you—so much sometimes that it hurts,” he huffed a wet laugh, eyes glassy as he pulled Mydei into his chest. 

Mydei closed his eyes, listening to the sound of his heartbeat, taking in a breath. “I love you too.”

They stayed like that for a while. No one teased, no one spoke. They were just two people in love in the middle of a celebration that couldn’t have gone any better. 

“Mama! Papa!” Augusta shouted, weaving through the other guests to barrel toward them. Mydei pulled back slightly to get a glimpse of her as Phainon knelt down to catch her in his arms. 

He lifted her up on one arm, letting her use both of them for balance as she held up a bouquet of flowers tied off with some twine and ribbon. “Look! I caught the flowers!”

“I see that,” Mydei chuckled, tucking a strand of her hair behind her ear.

“My baby’s too young to get married,” Phainon sniffled, wiping the corner of his eye playfully. 

Augusta giggled. “Silly papa. It means Mama’s next!” she chirped, pointing at him. 

Mydei’s eyes widened as their gaze met. Phainon flushed almost immediately, but Mydei just laughed lightly.

Augusta scrunched her nose, letting out a little hmph as Phainon leaned in to kiss Mydei’s cheek. 

“Yeah,” his voice was soft, eyes full of something unspoken, “we can make that happen.”
